pages.body:
# Front matter

**What this section holds.** 8 pages in this build. Pages marked FOR YOU matter most for your household and come first.

- → 00-01 **How to use this binder**: It explains what this binder is, how to find things in it on a phone with no internet, how each page is laid out, and how to keep it true as your household c…
- → 00-02 **Emergency quick reference**
- → 00-04 **Our family emergency and communications plan**: It is the household's one-page operating plan for being separated, reaching each other, getting the children, and leaving.
- → 00-05 **Safety disclaimer — read this first**: It tells you, in plain words, what this binder is, who checked it (a computer, not a person), what it can and cannot do for you, and which choices in it are …
- → 00-06 **The first 60 minutes**: The hour when something has just happened and nobody knows how bad it is.
- → 00-07 **Who does what: household roles and assignments**: It turns "we'll all pitch in" into named jobs, each with a backup, so nothing falls between people when everyone is tired, frightened or missing.
- → 00-09 **Your private copy: what it holds and why you must not share it**: It says what happened to the answers you typed, what is inside this file, and why the file is for your household only.
- → 00-10 **Keeping the binder alive: install it, print it, keep it charged**: This binder is one file.

pages.body:
# How to use this binder

> **If something is happening right now, stop reading this page.** Go to → 00-06 (the first 60
> minutes) or → 00-02 (emergency quick reference). This page is for a calm afternoon.

**What this page is for.** It explains what this binder is, how to find things in it on a phone
with no internet, how each page is laid out, and how to keep it true as your household changes.

## Do this now

1. **Read → 00-05 (the disclaimer) and → 00-09 (the private-copy notice).** Both are short. They
   are the frame for everything else.
2. **Install it properly** (→ 00-10): on more than one device, tested in airplane mode, with the
   key pages printed.
3. **Read Section 01, the phase playbooks.** Seven pages. Every other section hangs off them.
4. **Answer the decision cards you left open** (→ 30-02 to → 30-30). Any page that depends on an
   open card prints "Not decided yet".
5. **Count what you actually have** (→ 26-01, then → 22-04). Every runway in the binder needs that
   number.
6. **Put the quick-reference cards** (→ 25-08) where they belong: fridge, go-bags, vehicles.

## What this binder is

An offline survival reference for **{{ household.name }}**: {{ household.size }} people
({{ household.labels }}) with a home base in {{ home.county }}, {{ home.state_name }}. It was
generated from the answers you gave in settings, while the power and internet worked, for a time
when they do not. It assumes:

- **A long outage is possible**: weeks to months without power, phones, pharmacies or help.
  Short events are a smaller version of the same thing.
- **You may be new to all of this.** Every term is explained the first time it appears, or points
  to an explainer in Section 29.
- **You know your household better than the binder does.** Where a choice involves real risk, the
  binder explains it and asks you to decide (→ 30-02 to → 30-30).

**Everything is always included.** Your answers change the order and the wording: your home
region comes first, your household's medical conditions lead Section 02, your gear's pages lead
their sections. Nothing is left out because you did not tick it; a condition or a piece of gear
you add later is already in the binder.

## The three phases: the spine

{{figure fig-three-phases}}

| Phase | Meaning | Pages |
|---|---|---|
| **A** | **Shelter in place** at home for as long as home works | → 01-01 |
| **B** | **Movement**: the decision to leave, the route, the trip | → 01-02, → 01-03, → 01-07 |
| **C** | **Establish** at a destination, or anywhere you end up | → 01-04, → 01-05 |

{{#if has.destinations}}Your destinations, with their status (agreed, unannounced, property only
or undecided), are on → 01-05.{{else}}You have not entered a destination. → 01-05 explains why
that matters and what to do instead.{{/if}} The checklists for moving between phases are → 01-06.
Every topic page has a **Phase notes** block saying what changes in A, B and C.

## Finding things

- **Search** (the box at the top) searches every page, explainer, card and condition, offline.
- **The emergency row** at the top of every screen goes straight to → 00-02 and → 00-06.
- **Cross-references** look like `→ 08-02`. Tap one to go to that page. On paper, the number is
  the page id, in order.
- **The master index** (→ 00-03) lists every page; **the binder map** (→ 00-08) shows the sections
  and what each is for.
- **The region picker** in Section 32 shows any state's climate, hazards, radio frequencies and
  plants. Your home state comes first{{#if has.destinations}}, then your destinations'{{/if}}.
- **The condition picker** in Section 02 shows any medical condition in the library, not only the
  ones you ticked.

## Anatomy of a page

Every topic page has the same blocks in the same order, so you can find things by position even
when you cannot concentrate:

| Block | What it is for |
|---|---|
| **What this page is for** | One paragraph, plain words |
| **Safety callout** (if any) | The thing that will hurt you, and the floors that apply. Read it first |
| **Do this now** | The action list. **If you read nothing else, read this** |
| **Why / how it works** | The understanding, so you can adapt when reality differs |
| **Gear / items** | What to have now, and what to scavenge or substitute |
| **When it runs out** | How long it lasts, how to ration it, how to resupply, what replaces it |
| **Phase notes** | What changes in A, B and C |
| **Cross-references** | Where to go next |

### The header on every page

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Page id** (`NN-MM-slug`) | Stable. Cross-references use the `NN-MM` part |
| **Version and revised date** | If two copies disagree, the newer date wins |
| **Danger level** | `none`, `caution` or `critical` (below) |
| **Stamp** | "AI-reviewed, not human-verified" on every page (→ 00-05) |
| **Sources** | Title, publisher and date of each source. {{#if size.everything}}In your Everything binder every source document is bound behind the page that cites it.{{else}}{{#if size.large}}In your Large binder the documents cited by the life-safety sections (medical, water, food storage, fire and fuel, heating, power, first aid, hazards, children, radiation and chemical events, cards and floors) are bound behind the page; the others are in the Everything download (→ 00-09).{{else}}In the Small binder no document is inside; Large carries those behind the life-safety sections and Everything carries all of them (→ 00-09).{{/if}}{{/if}} |

### Danger levels

| Level | Meaning | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| **none** | Getting it wrong wastes time or money | Normal care |
| **caution** | Getting it wrong causes injury, illness or loss | Read the safety callout; follow the cited source |
| **critical** | Getting it wrong can **kill someone** | Read the whole page. Plan it with a professional now, while you can (→ 00-05). Examples: medicines, anaphylaxis, canning, carbon monoxide, water treatment, foraging, firearms, children's safety |

### Kinds of page

| Kind | What it means for you |
|---|---|
| **Core** | The same text in every household's binder. Method and facts that are true everywhere |
| **Region** | Filled from public datasets for your state and county |
| **Household** | Written from your answers: your plan, your people, your destinations. Only as good as what you typed |
| **Condition** | A medical module from the condition library (Section 02), with your own "my meds" rows |
| **Gear** | A module for a class of gear, with a spec row for your model or a blank to fill from the label |
| **Explainer** | Section 29: the words and ideas other pages assume |
| **Decision card** | Section 30: a real trade-off, with your household's answer |
| **Floors** | → 30-01: the rules that are never a choice |

More on what to trust, and why: → 29-15.

## Blanks, choices and photos

- **A blank line with "(fill in)"** means you skipped that question, or the binder will not guess
  it. Write it on the printed copy, and add it in settings next time you regenerate.
- **"Our choice:" lines** print your household's answer to a decision card, or "Not decided yet"
  with the card's page. Change a choice in settings, or cross it out on paper and write the new
  one with the date.
- **Photo frames** ("Add a photo in the app") are places to attach your own photo: the gas
  shutoff, the warm room, a meeting place. Photos stay on your device (→ 00-09, → 00-10).

## Reading it under stress: the three-layer rule

1. **Cards** (→ 25-08): ninety seconds, on the fridge and in every bag.
2. **"Do this now"**: the top block of the page you need.
3. **The rest of the page**: when there is time to understand, adapt and decide.

**Practise at layer 3 so you can act at layer 1** (→ 24-01).

## Keeping it current

The binder is regenerated, not edited. Keep your saved answers file (`profile.json`) somewhere
safe. When something changes, open the settings page, load that file, change the answer, and
generate a new binder. Then replace every copy (→ 00-10).

**Regenerate after:** a move; a new household member, baby or pet; a new medical condition or
medicine; new gear; a changed destination or contact; a changed decision card; and at the annual
review (→ 25-10).

**Write on the paper copy** in between: your measured water use, your frost dates, how much wood
a cold week took, what broke. Carry those notes into settings at the next regeneration. **A binder
that never changes is a binder nobody is using.**

### The habits that keep it true

| Cadence | What | Page |
|---|---|---|
| **Twice a year** (pick two dates, for example when clocks change) | Kit checks, expiry dates, children's sizes, full inventory | → 22-03, → 22-04 |
| **Twice a year** | A blackout weekend | → 24-04 |
| **Every three months** | One household drill | → 24-02 |
| **Each season** | That season's skills, garden and fuel | → 24-03 |
| **Once a year** | The full review, then regenerate | → 25-10 |

## Where to start, honestly

| If you have | Do this |
|---|---|
| **10 minutes** | Read → 00-06, and put the cards from → 25-08 on the fridge |
| **An hour** | Read Section 01 (the phases) and fill in → 00-04 (the family plan) |
| **An afternoon** | Walk the house with → 26-01 and → 26-02, then count everything into → 22-04 |
| **A weekend** | Run → 24-04, a blackout weekend. It finds more than anything else in the binder |
| **Some money** | Work down → 22-07 in order |
| **No money** | → 24-01 (skills), → 18-01 (neighbours), → 01-05 (secure a destination) |

## Gear / items

**Have now (buy toward this):** the binder on at least two devices; a power bank for each phone;
a printed copy of the key pages (→ 00-10) in a sturdy ring binder with tab dividers; sheet
protectors for pages that live in wet or greasy places (water, cooking, medical); sandwich bags or
a laminator for the cards; pencils (they write in the cold).

**Scavenge / substitute:** any folder or clip will hold paper. **What matters is that it is on
paper, in the house, where the family can find it in the dark.**

## When it runs out

Paper and files do not run out; **accuracy does.**

- **Runway:** about a year before medicines, contacts and children's sizes are noticeably wrong.
- **Ration:** if you can only keep part of it current, keep **your Section 02 condition pages,
  → 22-06 (the medical kit) and → 25-09 (the family medical summary)** current.
- **Resupply:** the twice-yearly checks, the annual review (→ 25-10) and regenerating.
- **Substitute:** none. **An out-of-date binder is a confident document full of stale facts**,
  which is worse than no document at all.

## Phase notes

- **A:** the whole binder is live. Read it, practise it, correct it.
- **B:** what you carry matters: the printed key pages, Section 01, your condition pages and the
  go-bag lists (→ 22-03, → 22-05). The binder device rides on a person, charged (→ 00-10).
- **C:** Sections 05, 06, 16 and 23 become the daily working pages. **Re-check everything
  local**: a new place changes the hazards, plants, frequencies and contacts. Use the region
  picker for your new county.

## Cross-references

- → 00-02 emergency quick reference · → 00-06 the first 60 minutes · → 00-05 the disclaimer
- → 00-09 the private-copy notice · → 00-10 install and charging
- → 00-08 the binder map · → 00-03 the master index · → 00-04 the family plan · → 00-07 roles
- → 29-15 how this binder was made · → 25-10 keeping it true

pages.body:
# Emergency quick reference

> **Find the row. Do the first action. Then go to the page.**
> This page gets you to the right page in under ten seconds. **The first action in each row is
> the one that must happen before you read anything.** For the first hour of a general emergency,
> use → 00-06 instead.
>
> **If phones are dead, every "call 911" below is replaced by the "No 911" action in the same
> row.** The first actions do not change; only the second half of the plan does. Decide now who
> runs to the neighbour with medical training (→ 18-01, → 25-03).

## Who in this household needs what

| Person | Role | Age | Conditions |
|---|---|---|---|
{{#each members as m}}| {{m.label}} | {{m.role}} | {{m.age_text}} | {{m.conditions}} |
{{/each}}

**Allergies:** {{#each allergies as a}}{{a.member}}: {{a.allergen}} ({{a.severity}}) · {{else}}none entered{{/each}}

**Medicines and what to do if doses are missed** are on → 25-09 and each condition's page in
Section 02. **Epinephrine is kept:** __________________________ **Glucagon or other rescue
medicine is kept:** __________________________

## Life-threatening: act before you read anything else

| If this is happening | Do this first | Then go to |
|---|---|---|
| **Anaphylaxis** (tight or hoarse throat, trouble breathing or swallowing, swelling of lips or tongue, many hives over the body, severe vomiting, fainting, often minutes after a food, sting or medicine) | **EPINEPHRINE INTO THE OUTER THIGH, NOW.** Then call 911. **A second dose if symptoms get worse, continue, or are not better in 5 minutes.** Antihistamines do not replace epinephrine (AAP, Allergy and Anaphylaxis Emergency Plan). *No 911: keep them lying on their back, or on their side if vomiting or struggling to breathe; stay with them and keep watching* | → 02-03 |
| **Severe bleeding** | **Hard direct pressure.** Life-threatening limb bleed: **tourniquet 2 to 3 inches above the wound (never over a joint), tight until the bleeding stops** (Stop the Bleed, USUHS). **Never loosen a tourniquet once placed while help can still come; mark the time. If no help will ever come, the conversion decision is DC-25 (→ 30-26).** *Our choice:* {{choice DC-25}} | → 12-02 |
| **Not breathing, no pulse** | **CPR. Call 911.** *No 911: CPR is unchanged; → 12-18 is the memory aid, → 12-16 the hard calls* | → 12-18 |
| **CO alarm, or several people with headache, nausea or dizziness at once** | **EVERYONE OUTSIDE. CALL 911. DO NOT GO BACK IN.** Turn a heater off only if it is within arm's reach on the way out. *No 911: fresh air is the treatment; rest outside for hours; find and stop the source, then air the house out before anyone goes back in* | → 08-02 |
| **Severe low blood sugar** (someone with diabetes is unconscious, seizing or cannot swallow) | **NOTHING BY MOUTH. Glucagon if they have it. Call 911.** *No 911: on their side; fast sugar only once awake and able to swallow; recheck in about 15 minutes and repeat until back in range* (CDC, Treatment of Low Blood Sugar) | → 02-01, → 02-05 |
| **High blood sugar with ketones, vomiting, belly pain, fruity breath or fast deep breathing** | **This may be DKA (diabetic ketoacidosis). Fluids. Get medical help** (CDC, Diabetic Ketoacidosis). *No 911: sick-day rules on the condition page; insulin is never stopped* | → 02-01, → 02-02 |
| **Choking** | **Coughing: let them cough. Silent: act.** Under 1 year: back blows and chest thrusts. 1 year and older: abdominal thrusts. *Goes limp: CPR* | → 12-18 |
| **Fire in the house** | **OUT. STAY OUT. Meeting place. Call 911.** *No 911: fight it only while it is small and contained, you have an extinguisher, and your exit is behind you (→ 29-12); past that, the house is lost, people are not* | → 29-12, → 24-02 |
| **Poisoning, swallowed something** | **Poison Control 1-800-222-1222** (America's Poison Centers). *No phone: do not make them vomit, keep the container, follow the label's first-aid statement* | → 12-17 |
| **Gas smell in the house** | **EVERYONE OUT** (FEMA, Utility Shut-off and Safety). **No light switches, no flames, no phones inside.** Call the gas emergency number from outside: {{ contacts.utility.gas.phone }}{{#if has.gas_any}} ({{ contacts.utility.gas.provider }}){{/if}}. Shut the gas at the meter only if you know how. If a propane heater was running from an outdoor tank, close the tank valve outside. Air the house out. FEMA says only a qualified professional turns the gas back on; relighting yourself when nobody will come is a household choice: {{choice DC-28}} (→ 30-29) | → 08-02, → 17-08 |
| **Tornado warning** | **Lowest floor, innermost room, no windows, cover heads.** Our spot: {{ dwelling.shelter_room }}{{#if has.mobile_home}}. **A mobile home is not a shelter: leave for a sturdy building before the storm** (NWS, Tornadoes: During the Event){{/if}} | → 17-02, → 17-06 |
| **Suicidal crisis** | **Stay with them. Call or text 988.** *No phone: never leave them alone, remove the means, get them through tonight* | → 12-15, → 21-03 |

## Urgent: minutes to hours

| Situation | First action | Page |
|---|---|---|
| **A medical device fails** (pump, oxygen concentrator, CPAP, monitor) | Go to the written backup plan on that condition's page | Section 02, → 09-06 |
| **Refrigerated medicine froze** | **A frozen-then-thawed insulin vial or pen is discarded**, even once, even if it looks normal: it loses strength with no way to tell (FDA, Insulin Storage in an Emergency). For other refrigerated medicines, follow the label (→ 29-07) | → 29-07, → 12-21 |
| **Refrigerated medicine got too warm** | Get it cool now (→ 12-21). Whether to use it past its published window is a household choice. **Our choice:** {{choice DC-08}} (→ 30-09) | → 30-09 |
| **Hypothermia** (shivering stops, confusion, clumsiness) | Get them dry, insulated and warmed gradually. **Handle gently** | → 08-05 |
| **Frostbite** | Do not rub. Rewarm only if it will not refreeze | → 08-05 |
| **Serious burn** | Cool with clean water. Cover. No ice | → 12-03 |
| **Broken bone, bad fall** | Keep it still. Check the circulation beyond the injury | → 12-09 |
| **Hit their head** | **Start the head-injury watch**; the red flags decide everything | → 12-19 |
| **Deep or dirty wound** | Wash it out thoroughly, dress it, **check for infection daily** | → 12-04, → 12-14 |
| **Dehydration, especially a child** | **Oral rehydration solution**, small sips, often | → 12-05 |
| **Stranded in a vehicle** | **STAY WITH IT** (Ready.gov, Winter Weather). Clear snow from the exhaust pipe before running the engine | → 22-05, → 01-03 |
| **Flooding** | **Never drive or walk into floodwater.** Go to high ground (NWS, Turn Around Don't Drown) | → 17-03 |
| **Someone at the door, a confrontation** | **Calm voice, distance, doors** | → 14-13, → 14-02 |

## System failures: hours to days

| Situation | First action | Page |
|---|---|---|
| **Power is out** | **Run outage day one.** Fill water containers now; fridge and freezer stay shut; medical devices first on any battery | → 09-16, → 00-06 |
| **Water is off or unsafe** | Use stored water; treat everything else. Know the water-heater and pipe reserves | → 03-02, → 03-04 |
| **We need heat, power out in winter** | **One warm room. CO alarm installed and tested BEFORE any fuel-burning heater is lit.** Only heaters rated for indoor use. Heat while people sleep is a household choice. **Our choice:** {{choice DC-01}} (→ 30-02) | → 08-01, → 08-04, → 08-02 |
| **No way to cook** | Fire, grill or camp stove **outdoors only** | → 07-01, → 07-02, → 07-05 |
| **Toilets do not work** | **Bucket toilet.** Stop flushing with drinking water | → 13-01 |
| **Freezer thawing** | Cook or preserve the contents, most perishable first | → 04-17, → 04-06 |
| **Fuel or wood running low** | Burn less first, then other fuels | → 06-04, → 06-05 |
| **Phones and internet down** | Weather radio, handheld radios, the written comms plan | → 15-01, → 15-03 |
| **A medicine or medical supply is running out** | **This is a reason to consider leaving, not just a rationing problem** | → 01-02, → 01-07 |

## Weather: this region

Your home county's hazards and their ratings, from the region data (Section 32):

| Hazard | Rating | Page |
|---|---|---|
{{#each region.home.hazards as h}}| {{h.name}} | {{h.rating_text}} | Section 17 |
{{/each}}

| Event | First action | Page |
|---|---|---|
| **Blizzard, extreme cold** | Stay put. One room. **Stay off the roads if at all possible** (Ready.gov, Winter Weather) | → 17-01, → 08-01 |
| **Tornado** | {{ dwelling.shelter_room }}, cover heads | → 17-02, → 17-06 |
| **Flood** | High ground. Never drive through water | → 17-03 |
| **Extreme heat** | Shade, fluids, cool cloths; watch children, elders and heat-sensitive medicines | → 17-04 |
| **Wildfire, grass fire** | Leave early. Do not wait to see | → 17-05 |
| **Long grid failure** | → 00-06, then Phase A | → 17-08, → 01-01 |
| **Illness outbreak** | Handwashing, distance, separate the sick | → 17-09, → 13-11 |

## Numbers

| Who | Number |
|---|---|
| **Emergency** | 911 |
| **Poison Control** | 1-800-222-1222 |
| **Suicide and crisis line** | 988 (call or text) |
| **Out-of-area contact**: {{ contacts.out_of_area.name }} | {{ contacts.out_of_area.phone }} |
| **Electric outages**: {{ contacts.utility.electric.provider }} | {{ contacts.utility.electric.phone }} |
| **Gas emergency**: {{ contacts.utility.gas.provider }} | {{ contacts.utility.gas.phone }} |
| **Water**: {{ contacts.utility.water.provider }} | {{ contacts.utility.water.phone }} |
{{#each local_contacts as c}}| {{c.name}} ({{c.relationship}}) | {{c.phone}} |
{{/each}}

Utility numbers are printed exactly as you typed them from your bills; the binder does not look
them up. State emergency management: {{ region.home.state_em }}. Weather office:
{{ region.home.nws_office }}. More numbers: → 25-03.

## The decisions

| Question | Page |
|---|---|
| **Do we stay or do we go?** | → 01-02: ask it every day |
| **Leaving with someone who has a medical need?** | → 01-07 |
| **How long do our supplies last?** | → 23-02, → 22-04 |
| **What do we do first, every day?** | → 01-01 |
| **What do we do about the children?** | Section 20, especially → 20-08 |
| **Who does what?** | → 00-07 |
| **A terrible medical call?** | → 12-16 |

## Five things to remember when nothing else comes to mind

1. **AIR, then BLEEDING, then WARMTH, then WATER, then FOOD.** In that order.
2. **Never burn anything indoors unless it is rated for indoor use and the CO alarm is up first.**
   Carbon monoxide kills silently (CDC, Carbon Monoxide Poisoning: Basics).
3. **Fill water containers early.** The window closes.
4. **Medicines that keep someone alive have no substitute.** They are the clock.
5. **Never ration:** drinking water, handwashing, medicine, children's food, sleep.

## Cross-references

- → 00-06 the first 60 minutes · → 25-08 the quick-reference cards · → 00-03 the full page index
- → 01-02 go/no-go · → 25-03 phone numbers · → 25-09 the family medical summary

pages.body:
# Our family emergency and communications plan

> **Fill this in, print it, and put a copy everywhere.** A plan that lives in one adult's head
> fails exactly when that adult is away, injured or unreachable. **Every blank on this page is a
> decision made now instead of under stress.** Blanks marked "(fill in)" are answers you skipped
> in settings; plain blanks are things the binder deliberately never asks a web page for.

**What this page is for.** It is the household's one-page operating plan for being separated,
reaching each other, getting the children, and leaving. Most of it was filled from your answers;
the rest you write by hand.

## Do this now

1. **Fill in every blank in one sitting.** Half an hour, and the most valuable half hour in this
   binder.
2. **Choose the out-of-area contact and actually ask them.** Someone far enough away not to be in
   the same event, willing to be the hub, who answers their phone. FEMA's advice: pick someone
   out of town, because they may be easier to reach in a disaster (FEMA/Ready.gov, Make a Plan).
3. **Walk to each meeting place** with everyone who would need to get there{{#if has.child}},
   children included{{/if}}.
4. **Make copies**: fridge, every go-bag, every vehicle, the out-of-area contact{{#if has.child}},
   and each school or daycare{{/if}}.
{{#if has.child}}5. **Teach each child their part** (section 8, → 20-04).{{/if}}

## Why / how it works

### The five decisions this plan makes in advance
1. **Where do we meet** if we are separated and cannot call?
2. **Who is the hub** everyone reports to?
3. **Who gets the children or dependants** if the usual adults cannot?
4. **What does a caregiver need to know** to keep everyone alive?
5. **Who does what** in the first hour (→ 00-07)?

**Text, do not call.** In an emergency phone lines may be tied up; a text may get through when a
call will not, and it leaves the lines open for emergency workers (FEMA/Ready.gov, Make a Plan).

## THE PLAN

Completed: ____________ · Reviewed: ____________ · Next review: ____________

### 1. Who we are

| Name | Role | Age | Conditions | Mobile phone | Work or school, and its phone |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
{{#each members as m}}| {{m.label}} | {{m.role}} | {{m.age_text}} | {{m.conditions}} | ____________ | ____________ |
{{/each}}

{{#if has.pets}}**Pets:** {{#each pets as p}}{{p.count}} {{p.type}} · {{/each}} Vet and phone: ______________________{{/if}}

Home address (write by hand, never typed into a web page): ______________________________________

### 2. Meeting places

{{photo meet-near-home}}

| | Place | Use it when |
|---|---|---|
| **1. Near home** | {{ contacts.meet.near_home }} | Fire or sudden evacuation of the house. **Go there and stay.** Never back toward the house, never behind a parked car where you cannot be seen |
| **2. In town** | {{ contacts.meet.in_town }} | You cannot get home. A house with people you know beats a landmark: it works at 2 a.m., in winter, in pyjamas. **Ask them first** |
| **Backup if 2 is unreachable** | ______________________ | |
| **3. Out of town** | {{ contacts.meet.out_of_town }} | You cannot get back into town |

### Making the plan real

A written plan that has never been walked is a wish. **Do these four things:**

1. **Walk to each meeting place** with everyone (→ 24-02).
2. **Run the 60-second grab drill**, timed (→ 22-03).
3. **Call the out-of-area contact and tell them what the role means.**
4. **Learn the shutoffs**: every adult, hands on the water main and the main breaker; at the gas meter, find the valve and the tool, but do not turn the gas off to practise (FEMA, Utility Shut-off and Safety).

## Gear / items

**Have now (buy toward this):** printed copies for every location in sheet protectors; wallet
cards with the out-of-area number for every adult{{#if has.child}} and child{{/if}}; a whistle for
each child; a magnet or clip for the fridge copy; the signed plans from your prescribers to attach.

**Scavenge / substitute:** an index card with **the out-of-area number, the meeting places, and
anyone's life-threatening allergy or condition** is most of the value of this page. Write it
today, put one in every wallet, and finish the rest later.

## When it runs out

- **Runway:** about a year. People move, numbers change, children's abilities change fast.
- **Ration:** if you fill in only two sections, fill in **2 (meeting places) and 5 (medical)**.
- **Resupply:** the annual review (→ 25-10), and regenerate after any move, new job, new school or
  new household member.
- **Substitute:** none. **An unwritten plan is a different plan in each adult's head**, and they
  disagree at exactly the wrong moment.

## Phase notes

- **A:** the plan covers ordinary emergencies too: a fire, a storm, a school lockdown, a hospital
  trip. That is most of its real use.
- **B:** sections 2, 3 and 6 are the operating plan. **The copies in the vehicles are the ones
  that matter.**
- **C:** rewrite it for the new place within the first week: new meeting places, neighbours,
  shutoffs, emergency numbers and weather radio frequencies (Section 32).

- → 20-04 teaching the children · → 24-02 drills · → 25-03 contacts · → 25-09 medical summary
- → 22-03 go-bags · → 25-08 the card version · → 01-05 destinations

pages.body:
# Safety disclaimer — read this first

**What this page is for.** It tells you, in plain words, what this binder is, who checked it (a
computer, not a person), what it can and cannot do for you, and which choices in it are yours to
make. Read it once, properly, before you rely on anything else in the binder.

> **This binder was assembled by an AI and reviewed by an AI. No doctor, nurse, engineer,
> electrician, lawyer or firearms instructor has checked your copy.** Every page carries the
> stamp "AI-reviewed, not human-verified", and the stamp means exactly that.
>
> **It is a reference for a time when no better reference exists:** when the phones, the
> internet, the pharmacy and the professionals are not available. While they are available, use
> them. **Where this binder and a professional disagree, the professional is right.**
>
> **You decide the risks.** Some pages offer choices that carry real danger. The binder explains
> them; the choice, and the responsibility for it, are yours. **You accept all risk from acting
> on this material.**

## Do this now

1. **Read the private-copy notice** (→ 00-09). It explains what the file contains and why you
   must not share it.
2. **Install the binder on more than one device and print the key pages** (→ 00-10). A binder
   on one dead phone is no binder.
3. **Read the floors** (→ 30-01). They are the few rules this binder never offers as a choice.
4. **Answer the decision cards you left open** (→ 30-02 to → 30-30). Every open card prints
   "Not decided yet" on the pages that depend on it.
5. **Book the real training** while classes exist: first aid and CPR, bleeding control, and
   anything your household's medical conditions need. No book replaces hands-on practice,
   including this one.
6. **Ask each prescriber now, while you can,** what to do if a medicine or device runs out or
   fails, and write the answer on that condition's page in Section 02.

## How this binder was made

Four kinds of material go into it (the full story is → 29-15):

| Part | Where it came from | How it was checked |
|---|---|---|
| **Core pages** (water, food, heat, first aid, and so on) | Re-written by an AI from one household's binder, whose facts were checked against their cited sources in November 2026 | AI review passes; never by a person for your copy |
| **Region pages** (climate, hazards, plants, radio frequencies) | Public datasets, by state and county | AI review passes against the datasets |
| **Household pages** (your family plan, roles, destinations) | Written by an AI from the answers you gave in settings | AI review passes; only as good as your answers |
| **Libraries** (medical conditions, gear, explainers, decision cards) | Written by an AI from cited public sources | AI review passes |

The review passes check that numbers on dangerous pages trace back to a cited source or to your
own answers, that one rule is stated the same way everywhere, that no blank was filled with a
guess, that nothing personal from another household survived, and that the writing is plain.
No person checks any of this, for the kit or for your copy.

**The known limit.** An AI review can catch a page that disagrees with its source. It cannot
catch a source that is wrong, or several sources that are all wrong in the same way. Only
experience and a professional can catch that.

## The pages that can kill someone if they are wrong

Treat these as **plan it with a professional now** topics, not **read it and do it** topics.
They are marked `critical` at the top of the page.

| Topic | Why | Who to plan it with now |
|---|---|---|
| **Medical conditions and their medicines** (Section 02) | Doses, timing and sick-day rules belong to one person and their prescriber | That person's prescriber and pharmacist |
| **Severe allergic reactions** (→ 02-03, → 02-04) | Anaphylaxis can kill in minutes; epinephrine comes first, and a second dose may be needed (AAP, Allergy and Anaphylaxis Emergency Plan) | The allergist |
| **Making water safe** (Section 03) | Wrong means disease; filtering and boiling do not remove salt or chemicals (US EPA, Emergency Disinfection of Drinking Water) | EPA and CDC guidance, as written |
| **Canning and preserving food** (→ 04-04, → 04-05) | Botulism gives no warning taste or smell; only tested processes are safe (National Center for Home Food Preservation, General Canning Information) | NCHFP or your Extension office, exactly as published |
| **Heating, fuel, generators and carbon monoxide** (Sections 06 to 09) | Carbon monoxide has no colour or smell and kills without warning (CDC, Carbon Monoxide Poisoning: Basics) | CDC guidance; the manufacturer's manual; a professional for installation |
| **Wild plants and mushrooms** (→ 05-06) | A wrong identification can kill and there is no antidote | A regional field guide **and** a person who knows |
| **Firearms** (Section 14) | Mechanical safety and the law both matter | The manufacturer's manual, a qualified instructor, current law |
| **First aid and medicines** (Section 12) | Use and dosing belong with a clinician | Your clinicians |
| **Children's safety** (Section 20) | Small children are the least resilient people in any house | Your pediatrician |
| **Radiation, chemical and biological events** (Section 27) | Timing and shelter decisions are unforgiving | Official instructions when they exist |

## Two kinds of safety rule: floors and decision cards

**Floors are not choices.** A floor is a rule where there is no safe way around it and the
failure is death or permanent injury without warning. The binder states each floor as a rule,
with the reason, on every page where it applies, and never prints a choice box for it. The full
list, with the reasons, is → 30-01. In short:

- Never run a generator, charcoal, or any engine indoors, in a garage, or near an open window.
- Never connect a generator to house wiring except through a transfer switch, or an interlock
  kit with the main breaker off. Never backfeed through an outlet with a double-male ("suicide")
  cord.
- Never loosen a tourniquet once placed while help can still come; mark the time. If no help
  will ever come, the conversion decision is DC-25 (→ 30-26).
- Low-acid foods are pressure-canned to the published time and pressure, or not canned.
- No wild plant or mushroom is eaten on a "test"; identification or nothing.
- Fuel is never stored or transferred near an open flame or a running appliance.
- A frozen-then-thawed insulin vial or pen is discarded.
- Bleach or pool shock is never mixed with ammonia, acids or other cleaners.
- Children do not have access to firearms, fuel, medications or chlorine products.

**Decision cards are choices.** Many survival questions are real trade-offs: an unvented heater
while people sleep, fuel in the car, medicine past its date. Each one has a card (→ 30-02 to
→ 30-30) that explains the hazard, what the manufacturer or agency says and why, how people get
hurt, what makes it safer, and the options. **Your household picks.** The binder prints your
answer wherever the trade-off comes up, and "Not decided yet" where you have not chosen. It never
presents another family's choice as the answer.

## What this binder deliberately does not contain

These are choices, not oversights:

- **No dose worked out for anyone.** The binder never calculates, adjusts or suggests a dose,
  ratio or schedule for a person's medicine. Where an agency or manufacturer publishes a table,
  it is printed as published, with the publisher named. Your own medicines appear exactly as you
  typed them from the bottle.
- **No canning time that a tested source did not publish.** Times depend on the food, the jar,
  the method and your altitude.
- **No ammunition reloading data.** That comes from current published manuals only.
- **No legal advice.** Where law matters, a short "Before the collapse" note says what the law
  was while government worked, and stops. A law never decides a survival procedure in this
  binder.
- **No made-up pictures for identification.** Plant and injury pictures come from published,
  attributed sources.
- **No web links.** There is no internet to look things up. Sources are named by title,
  publisher and date on every page. Which source documents are inside your file depends on the
  size you downloaded (below).

## Your answers, your file, and its size

- **Your answers are never stored.** There is no account and no database. Your answers were sent
  once, through a relay that checks your access key and keeps only a count of requests, to the AI
  service that wrote your binder. Nothing keeps them except this binder and, if you saved one,
  the answers file on your own device (→ 00-09).
- **Three sizes.** {{#if size.everything}}You downloaded **Everything**: every source document
  the binder cites is bound inside the file, behind the page that cites it.{{else}}{{#if size.large}}You
  downloaded **Large**: the source documents cited by the life-safety sections (medical
  conditions, water, food storage and canning, fire and fuel, heating, power, first aid, hazards,
  children, radiation and chemical events, decision cards and floors) are bound inside the file.
  Documents cited only by other sections are named by title and are in the **Everything**
  download.{{else}}You downloaded **Small**: no source document is inside the file; each one is
  named by title, publisher and date. **Large** binds the documents behind the life-safety
  sections, and **Everything** binds every one.{{/if}}{{/if}} The table is on → 00-09.
- **This file is private.** {{#if size.large}}It contains other people's copyrighted documents,
  fetched for your household's personal use, so giving it to anyone else breaks copyright.{{else}}It
  holds your family's private details, and a Large or Everything copy made from it would contain
  other people's copyrighted documents.{{/if}} **Do not share it** (→ 00-09).

## Using it safely: five rules

1. **Prefer the source over the summary.** Every page names its sources. If a page and its source
   ever disagree, the source wins and the page is wrong.
2. **Get the training now**, while classes, clinicians and hardware stores exist.
3. **When in doubt, do not.** In a real emergency the cautious option is usually right.
4. **Check your own answers.** Household pages repeat what you typed. A wrong phone number or a
   wrong medicine strength will be printed faithfully.
5. **Keep it current.** Write corrections on your printed copy, then change your answers in
   settings and regenerate (→ 00-01). A binder nobody corrects becomes fiction (→ 25-10).

## The honest limits

- **It cannot make insulin, epinephrine, infant formula or any other medicine**, and no skill in
  it can (→ 23-04). It can help you understand how long you have and use that time well.
- **It cannot replace surgery, imaging, blood, oxygen supply or a skilled birth attendant**
  (→ 12-16).
- **Region data is only as good as the public datasets.** Check it against local knowledge,
  especially hazards and plants.
- **It was written in 2026.** Products, laws and guidance change; the date on each page tells you
  how old it is.

## Cross-references

- → 00-09 the private-copy notice · → 00-10 install and charging · → 00-01 how to use the binder
- → 30-01 the floors · → 29-15 how this binder was made and what to trust
- → 12-16 the limits of care · → 25-10 keeping it true

pages.body:
# The first 60 minutes

**What this page is for.** The hour when something has just happened and nobody knows how bad it
is. Read it top to bottom, in order, and do it. The first hour is about **people, safety, water
and information**, in that order. Everything else can wait an hour; some of these cannot wait ten
minutes.

> **SAFETY — CRITICAL.**
> - **Never run a generator, charcoal, or any engine indoors, in a garage, or near an open
>   window.** Carbon monoxide kills in minutes with no warning; alarms fail; there is no
>   mitigation that works every time.
> - **Never connect a generator to house wiring except through a transfer switch, or an
>   interlock kit with the main breaker off. Never backfeed through an outlet with a
>   double-male ("suicide") cord.** It electrocutes line workers and neighbours and starts fires.
> - **Never loosen a tourniquet once placed while help can still come; mark the time. If no
>   help will ever come, the conversion decision is DC-25 (→ 30-26).** Re-bleeding and clot
>   release kill. **Our choice:** {{choice DC-25}}
> - **Fuel is never stored or transferred near an open flame or a running appliance.** Vapour
>   ignites.
> - **A frozen-then-thawed insulin vial or pen is discarded.** It loses strength with no way to
>   tell; the published guidance is unanimous.
>
> The reasons are on → 30-01.

## Minute 0 to 5: people and immediate danger

- [ ] **ACCOUNT FOR EVERYONE.** Say the names out loud: {{ household.labels }}.{{#if has.pets}} And the pets.{{/if}}
- [ ] **Anyone injured?** Bleeding first, always (→ 12-02, → 12-01).
- [ ] **Immediate hazard?** Fire, gas smell, structural damage, rising water, a tornado warning:
      **get out or get to shelter first.** Nothing on this page outranks that.
  - Fire: out, and stay out.
  - Tornado: {{ dwelling.shelter_room }}, cover heads (→ 17-02, → 17-06).
  - Gas smell: out, no switches, no flames.
- [ ] **CO alarm sounding, or anyone with headache, dizziness or nausea, especially several people
      at once: EVERYONE OUTSIDE, CALL 911, DO NOT GO BACK IN** (CDC, Carbon Monoxide Poisoning:
      Basics; → 08-02). No 911: fresh air is the treatment; rest outside for hours; stop the
      source before anyone goes back in.
- [ ] **Already leaving?** Go to → 22-03 (the 60-second grab) and → 01-06.

## Minute 5 to 10: medicine, before anything else

- [ ] **Find the medical kit** (→ 22-06). Put it where everyone knows, near the exit.
{{#if has.epinephrine}}- [ ] **Epinephrine:** confirm you have it, it is in date, and you can reach it (→ 02-03).{{/if}}
- [ ] **Refrigerated medicine: is it at a safe temperature right now?** (→ 29-07)
{{#each refrigerated_meds as x}}  - {{x.member}}: {{x.name}} {{x.strength}}
{{else}}  - No refrigerated medicine is entered. Check anyway: a new prescription may need it.
{{/each}}  - **Power is off:** keep the fridge shut. A closed fridge stays cold for about 4 hours
    (FoodSafety.gov, Food Safety During a Power Outage). If the outage looks long, move the
    medicine into a powered cooler or a cooling pouch before then (→ 09-16, → 12-21).
  - **Cold weather:** it must **not freeze**. Keep it inside, against the body if necessary.
  - **Hot weather:** get it out of the heat and into the coolest cooling you have (→ 12-21).
- [ ] **Devices that need power**{{#if has.oxygen}} (oxygen){{/if}}{{#if has.cpap}} (CPAP){{/if}}: check every battery. **Medical devices
      come first on every power bank and power station** (→ 09-06, → 09-10).
- [ ] **Count the days of each life-sustaining medicine on hand. Write the numbers down.**
      **The shortest one is the governing number for every decision that follows** (→ 01-02,
      → 23-01).

| Person | Medicine | Days on hand |
|---|---|---|
{{#each meds as x}}| {{x.member}} | {{x.name}} | ______ |
{{else}}| | | ______ |
{{/each}}

## Minute 10 to 20: capture water (the window closes fast)

- [ ] **Fill every container while the pressure lasts:** bathtub, pots, jugs, bottles, buckets
      (→ 03-02). Water pressure can fail hours after the power does. This window does not come
      back.{{#if has.well}} **A well pump stops when the power stops**: what is in the pipes and
      pressure tank is all you get (→ 03-10).{{/if}}
- [ ] **Know the reserves:** {{#if has.water_heater_tank}}the water heater (about
      {{ dwelling.water_heater_gallons }} gallons; know the drain valve), {{/if}}the water in the
      pipes, and ice in the freezer (FEMA, Food and Water in an Emergency). Toilet **tanks**
      (never the bowls) are the last reserve: FEMA says not to drink tank water, so keep it for
      flushing and washing, or disinfect it first if nothing else is left, and never if a
      cleaning tablet or dye is in it (→ 03-01, → 03-04).
- [ ] **Boil advisory or possible contamination?** Treat everything (→ 03-04).
- [ ] **Our numbers** (→ 03-01): drinking and minimal hygiene floor
      **{{ derived.water.floor_gal_day }} gallons a day** for this household; planning figure
      **{{ derived.water.plan_gal_day }} gallons a day**; stored water lasts about
      **{{ derived.water.stored_days }} days** at the floor.
- [ ] **Freezing risk and no heat?** Shut the water main and drain the pipes (→ 03-06, → 17-01).

## Minute 20 to 30: information and contact

- [ ] **Turn on the NOAA Weather Radio** (→ 15-01). What is actually happening? For how long?
      Our transmitters: {{#each region.home.nwr as t}}{{t.call}} {{t.freq}} MHz · {{/each}}
- [ ] **Local radio, any working channel.** Write down what you learn and the time (→ 25-05).
- [ ] **Text, do not call.** Message the out-of-area contact, {{ contacts.out_of_area.name }}:
      where you are, who is with you, that you are safe (→ 15-03).
- [ ] **Save phone battery from this moment:** airplane mode between check-ins, low-power mode,
      screen dim, no scrolling (→ 00-10).
- [ ] **Check on neighbours**, especially anyone elderly or alone. Two minutes now buys the
      relationship you may need for months (→ 18-01).

## Minute 30 to 45: stabilise the house

- [ ] **Fridge and freezer stay shut.** About 4 hours for the fridge, about 48 hours for a full
      freezer (FoodSafety.gov, Food Safety During a Power Outage; → 04-17).
- [ ] **Heat (cold weather):** pick **one room** and start closing the house down to it (→ 08-01).
  - **Only heaters rated for indoor use, and only after a CO alarm is installed and tested in that
    room** (→ 08-02, → 08-04).{{#if has.unvented_heater}} You own: {{#each heaters as hh}}{{hh.kind_text}} · {{/each}}(→ 08-09, → 08-10).{{/if}}
  - **Grill, camp stove, generator: never inside.**
  - A fuel-burning heater running while people sleep is a household choice.
    **Our choice:** {{choice DC-01}} (→ 30-02)
  - A propane cylinder larger than 1 lb inside the house is a household choice.
    **Our choice:** {{choice DC-02}} (→ 30-03)
  - Candles and open flames indoors are a household choice. **Our choice:** {{choice DC-20}} (→ 30-21)
- [ ] **Cool (hot weather):** lowest floor, shade, moving air, wet cloths; watch children, elders
      and anyone on heat-sensitive medicine (→ 17-04).
- [ ] **Light:** headlamps out, one per person; do not light empty rooms (→ 10-01).
- [ ] **Power priority:** 1. medical devices 2. light 3. communications 4. refrigeration
      5. everything else (→ 09-01).{{#if has.power_station}} Our power stations hold about
      {{ gear.station_wh_total }} watt-hours in total, very roughly {{ derived.station_fridge_days }}
      days of a full-size fridge (an estimate; → 09-03).{{/if}}{{#if has.generator}} The
      generator runs **outside only**, more than 20 feet from any window, door or vent (CDC,
      Carbon Monoxide Poisoning: Basics; → 09-04).{{/if}}
- [ ] **Secure:** doors locked{{#if has.garage}}, garage down{{/if}}{{#if has.vehicle}}, vehicles locked. Fuel level in each vehicle? (→ 22-05){{/if}}
{{#if has.pets}}- [ ] **Pets:** contained, fed, watered, carriers where you can reach them (→ 20-09).{{/if}}

## Minute 45 to 60: decide, and set the shape of the next day

- [ ] **Read the go/no-go triggers (→ 01-02)** and ask them honestly, out loud, together:
  - Is the house safe? Is there water? Can we stay warm (or cool)?
  - Are the medicines and medical supplies enough for how long this looks?
  - Is it safe to travel: weather, roads, daylight, everyone's condition?
  - **In a winter storm, stay off the roads if at all possible** (Ready.gov, Winter Weather).
    Leaving into the storm is usually the more dangerous option.
- [ ] **If staying:** Phase A (→ 01-01). Assign roles (→ 00-07). Start the daily log (→ 25-05).
- [ ] **If leaving:** → 22-03 (bags), → 22-05 (vehicle), → 01-03 (movement), → 01-07 (medical
      needs on the road). Medicine rides in the cabin with a person. Go early rather than
      perfectly.
- [ ] **Everyone eats and drinks something**, especially anyone with diabetes{{#if has.child}},
      the children{{/if}}{{#if has.pregnant}}, anyone pregnant{{/if}}{{#if has.nursing}}, anyone
      nursing{{/if}}.
{{#if has.child}}- [ ] **Tell the children what is happening**, calmly and truthfully, at their level (→ 20-08).
      Give each child old enough a real job. It is the best thing you can do for them right now
      (→ 20-07).{{/if}}
- [ ] **Write down** what happened, what you did, what you used, and the time (→ 25-05).

## What people get wrong in the first hour

| Mistake | Instead |
|---|---|
| **Waiting to see if it comes back on** | Fill water in the first twenty minutes. The window closes and does not reopen |
| **Opening the fridge to check** | Keep it shut: about 4 hours fridge, about 48 hours full freezer (→ 04-17) |
| **Bringing a grill, camp stove, generator or any heater not rated for indoors inside for heat** | **Never.** This is how people actually die in outages (CDC, Carbon Monoxide Poisoning: Basics). Indoor-rated heaters run only with the CO alarm up first (→ 08-02) |
| **Burning phone battery on news and social media** | One check, write it down, then save power (→ 00-10) |
| **Leaving into a storm because staying feels passive** | Stranded vehicles kill people. Stay unless the triggers say otherwise (→ 01-02, → 17-01) |
| **Forgetting the medicine that has no substitute** | Deal with its temperature and count it in the first ten minutes (→ 29-07) |
| **Rationing children's food or drinking water on day one** | **Never ration those** (→ 23-01) |
| **Telling the children nothing** | Calm truth beats an anxious guess. They already know something is wrong (→ 20-08) |

## After the first hour

- **Hours 1 to 6:** settle into Phase A (→ 01-01). Set up the one-room plan, sanitation
  (→ 13-01) and lighting. **Sleep is a resource** (→ 21-07).
- **Days 1 to 3:** count everything and work out how long it lasts (→ 22-04, → 23-02). Set a
  routine, children's first (→ 21-04, → 20-03).
- **Every day after:** ask the go/no-go questions again (→ 01-02). Log everything (→ 25-05).

## Cross-references

- → 00-02 the fuller quick reference · → 25-08 the quick-reference cards
- → 01-01 Phase A · → 01-02 go/no-go · → 01-03 movement · → 01-07 leaving with medical needs
- → 29-07 refrigerated medicines · → 08-02 carbon monoxide · → 03-02 capturing water
- → 09-01 power priorities · → 22-03 go-bags · → 25-05 the daily log

pages.body:
# Who does what: household roles and assignments

> **Roles are not about who is in charge. They are about speed and redundancy.** Two adults who
> each assume the other grabbed the medical kit is a real failure, and it happens in the first
> sixty seconds. **The rule that matters most on this page: every role has a primary and a
> backup, and the backup has actually done it.**

**What this page is for.** It turns "we'll all pitch in" into named jobs, each with a backup, so
nothing falls between people when everyone is tired, frightened or missing.

## Do this now

1. **Fill in the assignments below together**, out loud. Disagree now rather than later.
2. **Circle every role where the backup has never actually done the job.** That list is this
   year's cross-training plan (→ 24-01).
3. **Assign the 60-second grab exactly**: who takes which person, who takes the medical kit, who
   takes the documents{{#if has.pets}}, who takes the pets{{/if}} (→ 22-03).
{{#if has.child}}4. **Give each child old enough a real job** and let them own it (→ 20-07).{{/if}}

## Why / how it works

### Three rules
1. **Primary and backup for everything.** If only one person can do a thing, that thing fails the
   day that person is ill, away, injured or asleep.
2. **The backup must have done it, alone, at least once.** Watching does not count (→ 24-01).
3. **Unpleasant jobs rotate.** Waste duty, night watch and hand laundry are shared, or they breed
   resentment, and resentment is a real threat to a household under strain (→ 21-05).

### The one that is not optional

**Every adult must be able to run every life-sustaining routine in this household**: not "know
about it", **run it**, in the dark, at speed. Where the supplies are, what the backup plan is when
a device fails, what an emergency looks like and what to do, where the rescue medicine is, how the
cold chain works, and how many days of supply remain. A household where only one person can do
this has a single point of failure walking around in it, and that person is often the one the
emergency hits hardest.

{{ai roles-must-know}}

## Role assignments

Completed: ____________ · Reviewed: ____________

**Who we are:**

| Name | Role | Age | Skills |
|---|---|---|---|
{{#each members as m}}| {{m.label}} | {{m.role}} | {{m.age_text}} | {{m.skills}} |
{{/each}}

### The first sixty seconds (assign this precisely)

| Job | Primary | Backup | Practised? |
|---|---|---|---|
| Accounts for every person | ________ | ________ | ______ |
{{#each members as m}}| Gets {{m.label}} out | ________ | ________ | ______ |
{{/each}}| Grabs the medical kit | ________ | ________ | ______ |
| Grabs the go-bags | ________ | ________ | ______ |
{{#if has.pets}}| Gets the pets and carriers | ________ | ________ | ______ |
{{/if}}| Grabs documents and cash | ________ | ________ | ______ |
| Shuts off gas and water if needed | ________ | ________ | ______ |
| Drives | ________ | ________ | ______ |

(An adult who can get themselves out writes "self" on their own row.)

{{#if has.young_child}}> **Never leave "who carries the baby" or "who holds the little one's hand" unspoken.** It is the
> gap a grab drill finds most often (→ 24-02).{{/if}}{{#if has.mobility_aid}}
> **Anyone who uses a wheelchair or walker needs a named helper and a planned route out**,
> including stairs (→ 02-22).{{/if}}

### Daily operations (Phase A and C)

| Job | Primary | Backup | Practised? |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Medical**: medicines, devices, supply counts | ________ | ________ | ______ |
{{#if has.anaphylaxis}}| **Allergies**: safe food, labels, epinephrine | ________ | ________ | ______ |
{{/if}}| **Water**: treating, storing, hauling | ________ | ________ | ______ |
| **Fire and fuel**: wood, fire, cooking heat | ________ | ________ | ______ |
| **Cooking** | ________ | ________ | ______ |
| **Food**: inventory, rotation, rationing | ________ | ________ | ______ |
| **Sanitation**: waste, cover, disposal | ________ | ________ | ______ |
| **Hygiene and laundry** | ________ | ________ | ______ |
| **Power**: batteries, solar, charging (→ 00-10) | ________ | ________ | ______ |
| **Communications**: radio checks, weather, check-ins | ________ | ________ | ______ |
| **Security**: doors, awareness, watch | ________ | ________ | ______ |
| **Tools and repair** | ________ | ________ | ______ |
{{#if has.child}}| **Childcare**, by block of time | ________ | ________ | ______ |
| **Schooling and routine** | ________ | ________ | ______ |
{{/if}}{{#if has.elder}}| **Elder care**: medicines, warmth, falls | ________ | ________ | ______ |
{{/if}}{{#if has.pets}}| **Pets** | ________ | ________ | ______ |
{{/if}}{{#if has.livestock}}| **Livestock**: feed, water, shelter | ________ | ________ | ______ |
{{/if}}| **Garden and food production** | ________ | ________ | ______ |
| **Logs and inventory** (→ 25-05, → 22-04) | ________ | ________ | ______ |
| **Morale**: the deliberate good thing | ________ | ________ | ______ |

{{#if has.child}}
### The children's jobs (real ones: → 20-07)

| Child | Their jobs | What they know |
|---|---|---|
{{#each children as m}}| {{m.label}} ({{m.age_text}}) | 1. ____________ 2. ____________ 3. ____________ | Own name and the adults' names · meeting place · "tell a grown-up right away" |
{{/each}}{{#each teens as m}}| {{m.label}} ({{m.age_text}}) | 1. ____________ 2. ____________ 3. ____________ | The whole family plan (→ 00-04) and their part in the first sixty seconds |
{{/each}}

Ideas by age: carrying the lamp,
counting the pets, fetching from a low shelf, keeping the water log. **Infants and toddlers have
no jobs: they are carried, fed, kept warm and dry, and kept on their schedule.** Which dangerous
jobs (fire, fuel, tools, animals) children may do when hands are short is a household rule.
**Our rule:** {{choice DC-24}} (→ 30-25)
{{else}}
### Children's jobs

No children are in this household now. If children ever join it, give each one a real job and
see → 20-07 and → 30-25.
{{/if}}

### Decisions: who calls it

| Decision | Who decides |
|---|---|
| **Immediate safety** (fire, CO, tornado, an intruder) | **Whoever sees it. No discussion, no vote.** Everyone else follows |
| **Go or no-go** (→ 01-02) | All adults together, against the written triggers. If we cannot agree: ______________ (decide the tie-break now, for example "the more cautious option wins") |
| **Medical** | The person whose condition it is, unless they are impaired; then the backup, **following the written plan from the prescriber**, not their own judgement |
| **Rationing and supplies** | All adults, weekly, against → 23-02 |
| **Dealing with outsiders** | Primary: ____________ Backup: ____________ |

### Sleep and watch (the part people ruin)

**Sleep is a survival resource. Protect it on purpose** (CDC, About Sleep; → 21-07).

- Night care{{#if has.young_child}} for the little ones{{/if}}{{#if has.elder}}, and for elders{{/if}}: alternate nights? ______________
- If a watch is truly needed: shifts of ______ hours, rotating: ______________________
- **Nobody does back-to-back nights.** Exhausted people make fatal mistakes.

### When one adult is gone or down

| If this person is unavailable | Someone else must be able to | Who |
|---|---|---|
{{#each members as m}}| {{m.label}} | __________________________ | ________ |
{{/each}}

**Gaps we know about (be honest):** ____________________________________________

**Plan to close them this year:** ____________________________________________

### Roles that quietly matter

- **The one who writes things down.** Logs (→ 25-05) are how a household hands over cleanly.
- **The one who notices the mood.** Long events are lost to despair and conflict far more often
  than to running out of something (→ 21-02, → 21-05).
- **The one who makes the deliberate good thing happen**: the fire, the treat, the birthday
  (→ 21-06). Not frivolous; it is why people keep going.
- **The one who talks to the neighbours** (→ 18-01). Community is a survival system (CDC, About
  Social Connection).

## Gear / items

**Have now (buy toward this):** a printed copy of this page inside a cabinet door; a wall calendar
for rotations and watch shifts; and **the training that makes a backup real**: a first-aid class
for every adult, trainer devices for any rescue medicine (epinephrine, glucagon), and a run-through
of each device's failure plan with the prescriber (→ 24-01).

**Scavenge / substitute:** a list on the fridge in marker does the whole job. **The substitute for
assigned roles is arguing at the door**, and it costs more than any gear on this page.

## When it runs out

- **Runway:** assignments hold for about a year; they break sooner as children grow and as one
  adult gets more practised than another.
- **Ration:** never concentrate roles to save effort. That is exactly how a single point of
  failure forms.
- **Resupply:** review at the annual review and after any drill that exposed a gap (→ 24-02).
- **Substitute:** **cross-training.** It is the only real redundancy a household has.

## Phase notes

- **A:** roles are mostly about efficiency, and about making sure nothing falls between people.
- **B:** the first-sixty-seconds table **is** the plan. Rehearse it until it needs no words.
- **C:** roles become jobs (wood, water, garden, animals, repair, care) and the schedule matters
  more than the list. **Rotate the miserable ones.**

## Cross-references

- → 00-04 the family plan · → 00-06 the first 60 minutes · → 22-03 the grab
- → 20-07 children's jobs · → 21-05 conflict between adults · → 21-07 sleep
- → 24-01 cross-training · Section 02, the condition pages every adult must be able to run

pages.body:
# Your private copy: what it holds and why you must not share it

**What this page is for.** It says what happened to the answers you typed, what is inside this
file, and why the file is for your household only. It is the same notice you saw on the settings
page and on the download screen, printed here so it travels with the binder.

## Your answers are never stored

Nothing you typed on the settings page was saved by the people who run it. There is no account,
no database and no log of your answers. Your answers lived only in your browser tab while you
filled them in. If you chose to save a copy of your answers as a file on your own device (a
`profile.json` file), that file is yours and stays with you.

When you pressed **Generate**, your answers were sent once to the AI service that writes the
binder (Anthropic's Claude API), through a small relay program. The relay's only jobs are to
check your access key and pass the request along. It keeps a count of requests and nothing else.
Its source code is shown on the settings site so you can read what it does. Cloudflare, which
hosts the settings page and the relay, keeps its own standard request records (times, sizes,
rough location) like any web host; nobody has asked it to keep anything more. The AI provider's
own data-handling terms apply to that request; the people who run this kit do not control those
terms, and say so here rather than promise more than is true.

**Photos you add to the binder never leave your device.** They are attached in your browser and
saved into a new copy of the file only when you press "Save a new copy".

**Your saved answers file is private too.** It holds your household's names, ages, medical
conditions, medicines and plans. Keep it where you keep other private papers.

## This file is your private copy. Do not share it.

{{#if size.large}}
{{#if size.everything}}**You downloaded the Everything binder.** It contains the full text of every
document this binder cites{{else}}**You downloaded the Large binder.** It contains the full text of
the documents cited by the life-safety sections (medical conditions, water, food storage and
canning, fire and fuel, heating, power, first aid, hazards, children, radiation and chemical
events, decision cards and floors){{/if}}: appliance manuals, first-aid guides, fire-safety
standards, medical-society fact sheets, university publications, written by other people and
organisations. They were fetched for **your personal use** when you downloaded this file,
because in an emergency you need the whole document in your hand, not a web address that no
longer works.

Those documents are copyrighted by their publishers. Giving your binder file to someone else
copies their work without permission and breaks copyright. **Keep this file to your own
household.**
{{else}}
**You downloaded the Small binder.** It holds the kit's own text, your household pages, and
public-domain material such as the plant plates and the Air Force survival handbook in Section
31. No source document is bound inside it; each one is named by title, publisher and date on the
page that cites it.

**Keep it to your household anyway.** It is full of your family's private details: names, ages,
medical conditions, medicines, meeting places and plans. And if you later upgrade to Large or
Everything, that copy will contain other people's copyrighted documents fetched for your
personal use only, and sharing it would break copyright.
{{/if}}

**If a friend wants a binder,** do not send them yours. Ask the person who gave you your access
key to give them their own, and they can make a binder for their own household. Theirs will
carry their own region, their own medicines and their own choices, which yours does not.

## Small, Large and Everything, in one table

| | Small | Large | Everything |
|---|---|---|---|
| Every page, explainer, decision card, condition and gear module | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| The national region appendix and every plant plate | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Each source named by title, publisher and date | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Source documents bound behind the pages that cite them | None | Those cited by the life-safety sections; the rest are listed as in the Everything download | Every cited document |
| Topographic maps for your home county and destinations | No | Yes | Yes |
| Rough size (the download screen showed your file's own estimate) | 30 to 60 MB | about 200 to 450 MB | about 0.4 to 0.9 GB: meant for a laptop |
| Contains other people's copyrighted documents | No | Yes: private copy, do not share | Yes: private copy, do not share |

A household with Small or Large can upgrade later from its saved answers file and this binder file
without the pages being written again (→ 00-10).

## What this binder is, and is not

This binder was assembled and checked by an AI from a verified core text, public datasets and the
answers you gave. **No doctor, engineer, electrician or other professional has reviewed your
copy.** It is a reference for a time when the normal references, services and professionals are
not available. While they are available, use them. Where this binder and a professional disagree,
the professional is right.

Several pages ask you to choose between options that carry real risk. Those pages explain the
hazard, what the manufacturer or agency says and why, what reduces the risk, and the choices. The
choice is yours and so is the responsibility for it. The full statement is → 00-05.

## Cross-references

- → 00-05 the safety disclaimer · → 00-10 keeping the file on your devices
- → 29-15 how this binder was made · → 25-06 the list of sources

pages.body:
# Keeping the binder alive: install it, print it, keep it charged

**What this page is for.** This binder is one file. It only helps if it is on a device that is
switched on, or on paper, at the moment you need it. This page shows how to keep the file on more
than one device, how to open it with no internet, why you still want key pages on paper, and how
to ration phone and laptop batteries so the binder outlasts the outage.

> **CAUTION.** Lithium batteries (phones, laptops, power banks, power stations) can bulge, leak
> or catch fire if damaged or faulty. Charge them on a solid, flat surface: charging on a soft
> surface such as a bed, pillow or couch, or blocking the vents, raises the fire risk. **If a
> battery is smoking, hissing, punctured or swollen, stop using it at once** (US Fire
> Administration, Lithium-Ion Batteries). If you can do it safely, move it away from anything that
> can burn.

## Do this now

1. **Copy the file onto at least two devices**: a phone for each adult and one laptop or tablet.
   {{#if has.teen}}A teenager's phone is a good third copy.{{/if}}
2. **Turn on airplane mode and open the file on each device.** If it opens, searches and turns
   pages with no connection, that copy is real. If not, fix it now (below).
3. **Press the PDF export button and print the key pages** listed below. Put them in a binder
   with sheet protectors.
4. **Choose the binder device** (below) and keep its battery for the binder and medical apps.
5. **Start the power-bank rotation** (below) today, while the grid works.

## Where the file lives

The binder is a single web-page file. It opens in the phone's or computer's web browser, but it
does not need the internet: everything (pages, pictures, search{{#if size.large}}, and the source
documents bound in your download{{/if}}) is inside the file.

- **Keep the file on the device itself, not only in a cloud folder.** A file that lives only in an
  online storage service is not on your phone when the network is down. In your phone's file app,
  check that the file is stored on the phone, or marked as downloaded for offline use.
- **Check the free space.** Roughly: Small 30 to 60 MB, Large 200 to 450 MB, Everything 0.4 to
  0.9 GB (meant for a laptop; → 00-09). Phones that are nearly full delete "offloaded" files
  without asking.{{#if size.everything}} Your Everything file may be too big for some phones: keep
  it on the laptop and put a Small or Large copy on each phone.{{/if}}
- **One copy on a memory stick or SD card** in the go-bag or the document kit (→ 19-01) is a cheap
  extra copy for a borrowed laptop.
- **An old phone or tablet in a drawer**, charged, with the binder on it and nothing else, is a
  spare that nobody drains. For protecting a spare device from a solar storm or EMP, see → 27-03.

## Opening it offline

- Open the file from the file app. If the phone offers several apps, choose a web browser.
- The pages are readable even where the browser does not run scripts. **Search, the region
  picker, the condition picker, photo slots and PDF export need the browser to run scripts**; a
  full web browser does.
- **Test in airplane mode on every device, every time you replace the file.** Untested copies fail
  at the worst moment.
- The binder opens in a dark theme to save battery. Turn the screen brightness down as far as you
  can still read.

## Updating, and which copy wins

- When you change your answers in settings and generate again, **replace every copy**: every
  phone, the laptop, the memory stick. Delete the old file so nobody opens it by mistake.
- The date on the cover and the `revised` date on each page tell you which copy is newer. **If two
  copies disagree, the newer one wins.**
- **Photos you attach** stay inside the copy where you attached them only after you press "Save a
  new copy". Save, then put that new copy on the other devices.
- **Small, Large and Everything.** Small has no source documents inside; Large binds those cited
  by the life-safety sections; Everything binds all of them. You can upgrade later from your saved
  answers file and this binder file without the pages being written again (→ 00-09).

## Why a printed copy still matters

Phones run out of charge, break, get wet, get lost, and slow down in hard cold. Paper does none of
that. It can be read by headlamp, by a child, by a neighbour who has never seen your phone, and by
two people at once.

The **PDF export button** turns the binder into printable pages (a file you print while the
printer and power still work). You do not need to print all of it. Print these first, in this
order:

1. → 00-02 emergency quick reference and → 00-06 the first 60 minutes
2. → 00-04 your family plan, one copy for every go-bag and vehicle
3. → 25-08 the quick-reference cards (cut out, for the fridge, bags and vehicles)
4. → 25-09 the family medical summary, and the Section 02 page for every condition your household
   has
5. → 30-01 the floors and your own decision cards
6. Section 01 (the phase playbooks) and → 09-16 outage day one

Then, if you can, the rest. Write on the paper copy as you learn things, and carry the corrections
into settings the next time you regenerate.

## Which device holds the binder

Decide this now, out loud, so nobody drains the binder phone scrolling news.

| Device | Job in an outage | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **The binder device** (one phone or tablet) | The binder, and medical apps that must keep running | Kept in airplane mode except at agreed check-in times; charged first after medical devices |
| **Each other phone** | Messages and calls at the agreed check-in times (→ 15-03) | Airplane mode between check-ins |
| **Laptop** | Reading the binder at home when a power station or generator is running; printing while there is power | Big battery, but it uses far more power than a phone; do not run it for comfort |
| **A spare device in a drawer** | Backup binder | Charge it with the rest; do not use it |

If a household member's medical device or app runs on a phone (for example a glucose monitor or
pump app), **that phone is a medical device first** and does not double as the binder device
(→ 09-06).

## Charge discipline

**Power priority in an outage:** medical devices first, then light, then communications, then
everything else (→ 09-01, → 09-06).

### While the grid still works
- Keep phones, laptops and power banks topped up as a habit. When an outage starts, **charge
  everything to full while the power flickers** (→ 09-16).
- **Recharge stored power banks every few months**, because lithium batteries slowly lose charge
  in a drawer. Follow each manufacturer's storage instructions.

### Power-bank rotation
{{figure fig-power-bank-rotation}}

Number your power banks. At any moment:

- **one is in use** (in a pocket, charging a phone),
- **one is charging** (from a power station, a solar panel, or a vehicle that is running anyway),
- **one is full and set aside** as the reserve.

When the one in use is empty, it goes to charging; the charging one, when full, becomes the
reserve; the reserve goes into use. Write the number and the date on a strip of tape when each one
is filled. If you own only one power bank, keep it full and use it only for the binder device and
medical devices.

{{#if has.power_station}}
**Your power stations** (about {{ gear.station_wh_total }} watt-hours in total) can refill power
banks and phones many times over. Charge small batteries from them in daytime, when solar can
refill the station (→ 09-03, → 29-02).
{{else}}
**Without a power station,** refill power banks from a vehicle only when the vehicle is running
for another reason, outdoors, and never in a garage (carbon monoxide; → 08-02). Solar chargers
and hand-crank radios with a charging port are the other options (→ 09-11).
{{/if}}

### Make each charge last
- **Airplane mode is the biggest single saving.** A phone with weak or no signal burns battery
  searching for a tower. Turn airplane mode on, and turn it off only at agreed check-in times to
  send and receive messages (→ 15-03).
- **Turn off Wi-Fi, Bluetooth and location** unless a medical device needs them.
- **Turn on the phone's low-power or battery-saver mode.** It slows background activity.
- **Dim the screen** and keep the binder's dark theme. Close other apps. No video, no games.
- **Text, do not call.** Texts get through on a busy network and use less battery.
- **Keep batteries warm in cold weather.** Lithium batteries lose usable charge in the cold and
  recover when warmed. Carry the phone in an inside pocket, and warm a cold battery before
  charging it (→ 09-07).
- **Keep them out of heat.** Do not charge them in direct sunlight (US Fire Administration,
  Lithium-Ion Batteries), and do not leave them in a parked car in the sun.

### Charging safely
- Use only the original charger and cable, or a certified replacement; avoid cheap knockoffs
  (US Fire Administration, Lithium-Ion Batteries).
- Charge on a solid, flat surface, never under a pillow or on a bed or couch.
- A battery that has been crushed, punctured, soaked or overheated is not trusted again.

## The charge-discipline card

Copy this onto a card for the fridge and every go-bag (→ 25-08):

| | |
|---|---|
| **Binder device** | ______________________ |
| **Check-in times** | ______________________ |
| **Power banks** | Numbered 1 to ___ · one in use, one charging, one full |
| **Between check-ins** | Airplane mode · low-power mode · screen dim |
| **Charge order** | Medical devices → binder device → lights → radios → other phones |
| **Never** | Charge on a bed · run an engine indoors to charge anything |

## Cross-references

- → 00-01 how to use the binder · → 00-09 the private-copy notice
- → 09-01 power priorities · → 09-06 charging medical devices · → 09-16 outage day one
- → 09-07 batteries in cold and heat · → 27-03 protecting electronics · → 29-02 batteries explained

- → 01-01 **Phase A: shelter in place**: How to stay at home and make it work when the power, water, phones or shops fail.
