pages.body:
# Lifecycles of every major consumable

**What this page is for.** Every supply in the house moves through the same four stages, from
a pile that only shrinks to something you can make for yourself. This page shows the **shape**
of each problem and where your household stands. It holds no burn rates, doses or mixing
ratios: each row points to the page that has the real numbers, limits and method.

> **Caution.** Do not plan a fuel burn rate, a medicine dose or a chlorine dilution from this
> page. Follow the cross-reference.

## Do this now

1. **Read the four stages once.** They are the same for every supply, and knowing them turns
   "we are running out of X" into a decision.
2. **For each row below, mark the stage you are really at today.** For most things in most
   houses the honest answer is **stage 1: stock only**. That is the finding.
3. **Pick the three rows where stage 2 or 3 is cheapest to reach** and buy or learn toward them
   this year (→ 22-07). For most households: water treatment, fuel or firewood, and garden seed.
4. **Accept the class C rows.** Prescription medicines the body depends on, epinephrine and
   infant formula have **no stage 2, 3 or 4**. They only have stock. That is why the
   leave-or-stay plan exists (→ 01-02).

## The four stages every supply passes through

{{figure fig-four-stages-of-a-resource}}

| Stage | What it means | What it costs you |
|---|---|---|
| **1. Stock** | You have a pile. It only shrinks | Nothing now; it ends on a fixed date |
| **2. Extend** | Ration, recover, reuse, repair. The pile shrinks more slowly | Discipline and work |
| **3. Substitute** | Something else does the job, usually worse (→ 23-03) | Some quality, comfort or safety |
| **4. Produce** | You make or gather it, on and on | Land, tools, skill and a lot of time |

**A supply is only really solved at stage 4.** Stages 2 and 3 buy time to get there. A supply
with **no stage 4** has a deadline, and the deadline sets the plan.

**The most useful question on this page:** for this supply, what does stage 4 actually
need, and do we have it here, on this property, in this {{ home.setting }} setting? Many stage 4
answers need land, wood, water and space that a town lot does not have. If that is true for
you, it is the case for a destination (→ 01-05), stated as an inventory rather than a fear.

Each row below gives: **Stock**, **Runway** (how long the stock alone lasts at normal use),
**Extend**, **Substitute**, **Produce**, **Stage 4 needs**, a **Verdict**, and where the real
numbers are.

## Water

| | |
|---|---|
| **Stock** | Stored containers, the water-heater tank{{#if has.water_heater_tank}} ({{ dwelling.water_heater_gallons }} gal){{/if}}, the pipes{{#if has.pool}}, the pool or hot tub ({{ dwelling.pool_gallons }} gal, not drinkable as it stands){{/if}} |
| **Runway** | Days on stored water (yours: about {{ derived.water.stored_days }} days at the floor, → 23-02) |
| **Extend** | Stop flushing with drinking water; catch every drop; reuse wash water (→ 13-03) |
| **Substitute** | Snow and ice melt (→ 03-06), rain (→ 03-05), surface water as a last resort, treated (→ 03-04). Drinking pool or surface water: {{choice DC-13}} → 30-14 |
| **Produce** | Rain catchment plus a treatment chain you can run indefinitely: filter, then boil or disinfect (EPA, Emergency Disinfection of Drinking Water; → 03-04) |
| **Stage 4 needs** | A roof, gutters, barrels, and either fuel for boiling or a lasting filter with spare elements{{#if has.well}}. Your well also needs a way to draw water without power (→ 03-10){{/if}} |
| **Verdict** | **Reachable almost anywhere it rains or snows.** Water is the supply most households can solve where they are |
| **Where the numbers are** | → 03-01 needs · → 03-04 treatment · → 03-03 pool · → 03-06 winter · → 03-08 keeping it good · → 03-10 a well without power |

## Heat and cooking fuel: wood

| | |
|---|---|
| **Stock** | The woodpile ({{ gear.fuel.firewood_cords }} cords in settings) |
| **Runway** | **Short.** A stack sized for occasional fires disappears fast once it is your only heat and cooking fuel (MU Extension, Wood Fuel for Heating) |
| **Extend** | Burn for work, not looks: contained fire, cook and heat with the same burn, heat one room (→ 08-01), bank the coals, cook in bulk (→ 07-01) |
| **Substitute** | Fallen wood, scrap lumber, pallets, paper logs. **Never burn painted or pressure-treated wood indoors** (→ 06-04) |
| **Produce** | Cut, split and **season** wood. Seasoning takes months, so wood cut today is next winter's fuel, not tonight's |
| **Stage 4 needs** | **Standing timber you have the right to cut**, an axe and saw and the skill to use them (→ 16-06), and a dry stack with a year of lead time |
| **Verdict** | {{#if has.acreage}}**Possibly reachable** if your land carries enough timber. Work it out on → 06-04.{{else}}**Usually not reachable in a town or suburb.** There is rarely a lasting in-town firewood supply. For many households this is the strongest depletion argument for a rural destination (→ 01-05).{{/if}} |
| **Where the numbers are** | → 06-01 fire · → 06-04 wood supply · → 07-01 cooking fire · → 16-06 axes and saws · → 08-08 wood heat |

## Liquid fuels and propane

| | |
|---|---|
| **Stock** | Gasoline {{ gear.fuel.gasoline_gal }} gal, diesel {{ gear.fuel.diesel_gal }} gal, kerosene {{ gear.fuel.kerosene_gal }} gal, propane {{ gear.fuel.propane_20lb }} × 20-lb and {{ gear.fuel.propane_1lb }} × 1-lb (from settings) |
| **Runway** | Hours of running time per gallon or cylinder, from each appliance's label or manual. **And a shelf life** (below) |
| **Extend** | Run engines and heaters only for a purpose, at the setting the manual gives; share one burn for several jobs |
| **Substitute** | Wood, solar, doing without (→ 23-03). Never a different fuel in an appliance not built for it |
| **Produce** | **Not possible at household scale** |
| **Stage 4 needs** | A working fuel supply chain |
| **Verdict** | **Stock only, and some of it ages.** See below |
| **Where the numbers are** | → 06-06 storage · → 09-04 generators · → 08-10, → 08-09 heaters · → 29-01 what each fuel is |

**How long stored fuel lasts.** There is no federal or manufacturer shelf-life number for
stored gasoline, kerosene or diesel that you can plan on. What can be said:
- **Untreated gasoline keeps for months, not years.** It loses the parts that help an engine
  start, can take up water, and leaves gum in small engines. Stabiliser added when it is fresh
  slows this.
- **Kerosene and diesel** age more slowly but take up water and grow sludge in part-full cans.
  One common wick-heater maker says never use kerosene stored from one season to the next
  (GHP Group/Dyna-Glo, kerosene heater owner's manual).
- **Propane does not go stale.**

Whether your household burns old fuel, and how old, is a decision card: {{choice DC-17}}
→ 30-18. Date every can when you fill it (→ 26-08).

## Food

| | |
|---|---|
| **Stock** | The pantry, plus the freezer (which is on a clock the moment the power goes) |
| **Runway** | Whatever your counted calories say (→ 04-01; your daily need is about {{ derived.calories.day }} kcal). Count it, do not estimate it |
| **Extend** | Eat the freezer first, keep portions steady, **never ration children's food** (→ 23-01), preserve freezer food before it spoils (→ 04-17) |
| **Substitute** | Sprouts for fresh food in winter (→ 04-16); wild greens as an extra only, identified with certainty (→ 05-06) |
| **Produce** | Garden, chickens or rabbits, hunting, fishing, trapping, each with its own season and lead time |
| **Stage 4 needs** | Garden space and **soil built over years** (→ 05-11), **seed you can save** (→ 05-03), water for the garden, animal protein, and a way to preserve the harvest (→ 04-04) |
| **Verdict** | {{#if has.acreage}}**Partly to largely reachable** on acreage, with years of work.{{else}}**Partial.** A yard can grow real vegetables and eggs; it cannot grow a year of calories for {{ household.size }} people. Grain and fat are the gaps.{{/if}} |
| **Where the numbers are** | → 04-01 pantry math · → 04-19 freeze-dried food · → 05-01 garden · → 05-03 seed saving · → 05-07 hunting |

## Light

| | |
|---|---|
| **Stock** | Flashlights, headlamps, batteries, candles, lamp oil |
| **Runway** | Longer than people expect if you use LEDs first and stop lighting empty rooms (→ 10-01) |
| **Extend** | One light per task, not per person; rechargeables plus a small panel; go to bed with the dark |
| **Substitute** | Fat and oil lamps, homemade candles, firelight (→ 10-03, → 10-04) |
| **Produce** | Rendered fat into candles and lamp oil; cotton wicks. Lasting, and dim |
| **Stage 4 needs** | A fat supply (which means animals, which means stage 4 food) and wick material |
| **Verdict** | **Reachable, at a quality cost.** Light fades gradually rather than ending |
| **Where the numbers are** | → 10-01 · → 10-03 · → 10-04 |

## Electricity

| | |
|---|---|
| **Stock** | Power stations ({{ gear.station_wh_total }} Wh in settings), power banks, vehicle batteries |
| **Runway** | Days, and less in cold (→ 09-07). A full-size fridge alone: about {{ derived.station_fridge_days }} days with no sun (estimate; the battery's own screen is the truth) |
| **Extend** | Triage the loads: **medical devices first, everything else negotiable** (→ 09-01) |
| **Substitute** | Vehicle charging (engine outdoors only), hand crank, doing without |
| **Produce** | Solar panels, a charge controller and a battery bank (→ 09-02, → 09-09). Yours: {{ gear.solar_w_total }} W of panels |
| **Stage 4 needs** | Panels, a controller, a battery you can replace, and **winter reality**: December output is a fraction of June's (→ 09-05). Your rough clear-day estimate: {{ derived.solar_wh_dec }} Wh in December, {{ derived.solar_wh_jun }} Wh in June |
| **Verdict** | **Reachable now, fading later.** Panels last decades; **the batteries are the consumable**, and they are stage 1 with no stage 4 |
| **Where the numbers are** | → 09-01 load triage · → 09-02 solar · → 09-03 batteries · → 09-05 winter · → 09-10 medical power |

## Sanitation and hygiene

| | |
|---|---|
| **Stock** | Soap, bleach, toilet paper, wipes, bin bags{{#if has.cats}}, cat litter{{/if}} |
| **Runway** | Weeks. **Bin bags and bleach run out sooner than you expect**, and both carry a lot of weight in the plan |
| **Extend** | Wash hands with less water, not less often. **Hygiene is never the thing you ration** (→ 13-02) |
| **Substitute** | Boiled cloth wipes, wood ash for scouring, ash or lime in the latrine (→ 13-07) |
| **Produce** | **Soap from fat and lye** (→ 13-09): a real stage 4 and one of the most valuable skills in the binder |
| **Stage 4 needs** | Fat, hardwood ash for lye, a container, and the method done carefully: **lye burns skin and eyes** |
| **Verdict** | **Reachable.** Soap-making is where a skill truly replaces a supply chain |
| **Where the numbers are** | → 13-02 · → 13-09 · → 13-01 · → 13-11 |

## Clothing, bedding, footwear

| | |
|---|---|
| **Stock** | What is in the closets{{#if has.child}}, and **the children grow out of theirs on a schedule**{{/if}} |
| **Runway** | Months to a year before wear matters{{#if has.child}}; **the children's sizes are the real clock**{{/if}} |
| **Extend** | Repair before replacing (→ 16-04), rotate to dry (→ 11-03), keep feet dry (→ 11-04) |
| **Substitute** | Layers, quilts, a blanket made into a garment, adult wool cut down for a child |
| **Produce** | Sew and patch from salvaged cloth. **Making new cloth is not realistic** |
| **Stage 4 needs** | Needles, thread and salvage. Plan on salvage for good |
| **Verdict** | **Salvage-dependent, permanently.**{{#if has.child}} Buying the next two sizes up of children's clothing and boots now is one of the cheapest hedges in this binder (→ 11-09).{{/if}} |
| **Where the numbers are** | → 11-01 · → 11-02 · → 11-07 · → 16-04 |

## Tools, blades, fasteners

| | |
|---|---|
| **Stock** | The tools in the house and garage |
| **Runway** | Years for good steel; **the consumables around them go first**: files, saw blades, fuel, screws, tape |
| **Extend** | Sharpen and maintain (→ 16-02), use the right tool, store dry |
| **Substitute** | Hand tools for power tools (→ 16-01), cord for hardware (→ 16-03) |
| **Produce** | Basic forge and repair work (→ 16-08). Realistically you reuse rather than make |
| **Stage 4 needs** | Fire, an anvil surface and skill: a long apprenticeship for modest results |
| **Verdict** | **Buy quality once.** A good axe, a good file and a good knife outlast almost everything else here |
| **Where the numbers are** | → 16-01 · → 16-02 · → 16-06 · → 16-08 |

## Medical: class C

| | |
|---|---|
| **Stock** | Prescription medicines, device supplies, epinephrine, formula, first-aid supplies |
| **Runway** | **For most households with a daily prescription, the governing clock.** Yours: {{#each meds as m}}{{m.name}} ({{m.member}}) about {{m.days_on_hand}} days; {{else}}none entered in settings; {{/each}}see → 23-02 |
| **Extend** | Correct storage (→ 29-07, → 12-21) and building supply legitimately while pharmacies work (→ 12-07). **Stretching doses is not a household decision**: ask the prescriber now |
| **Substitute** | **None for insulin, epinephrine or most daily prescriptions. None for a skilled birth attendant or surgery** (→ 23-03) |
| **Produce** | **Impossible**, at any scale, by any skill |
| **Stage 4 needs** | A working pharmaceutical industry |
| **Verdict** | **No lifecycle: only a stock and a date.** That is why the leave-or-stay decision exists (→ 01-02), why the medical go-kit is packed first (→ 22-06), and why getting supply back is a goal, not a chore |
| **Where the numbers are** | → 12-07 · → 12-11 · → 02-01 · → 02-03 · → 12-01 · → 12-16 · → 23-02 |

## Ammunition

| | |
|---|---|
| **Stock** | What is on the shelf, by calibre{{#if !has.firearms}} (none, per settings){{/if}} |
| **Runway** | Long for defence, **short for hunting** if hunting becomes a food plan |
| **Extend** | Practise with the cheapest calibre; confirm your sights once rather than re-adjusting again and again (→ 14-09) |
| **Substitute** | Traps and snares, which keep working while you do other jobs and use no ammunition (→ 05-15) |
| **Produce** | Reloading only moves the problem: its parts are a stock too. **No load data appears in this binder** |
| **Stage 4 needs** | Press, dies, primers, powder, bullets; primers are the hard stop |
| **Verdict** | **Finite. Treat every round as irreplaceable**, and let traps feed you |
| **Where the numbers are** | → 14-07 · → 14-08 · → 14-09 · → 05-15 |

## Seed, soil and fertility

| | |
|---|---|
| **Stock** | The seed packets in the drawer and what the soil holds now |
| **Runway** | Seed germination drops each year; **soil fertility drops with every harvest** |
| **Extend** | Store seed cool, dark and dry; compost everything (University of Minnesota Extension, Composting in Home Gardens; → 05-11); rotate beds |
| **Substitute** | Buy open-pollinated varieties now: **hybrid seed does not come true from saved seed** (→ 05-03) |
| **Produce** | **Save seed** and **build soil**: compost, ash, mulch; human waste only within → 13-06's limits |
| **Stage 4 needs** | Open-pollinated varieties, distance between some crops so they do not cross, drying and storage, years of compost |
| **Verdict** | **Reachable, but only with a head start of several years.** Seed and soil cannot be bought in a hurry, which makes them the best thing to spend this year on |
| **Where the numbers are** | → 05-03 · → 05-11 · → 05-02 · → 25-01 |

## Money and records

| | |
|---|---|
| **Stock** | Cash on hand and the document kit (→ 19-01) |
| **Runway** | Cash is useful early and worthless late; documents stay useful |
| **Extend** | Small bills; spend cash while it is still accepted |
| **Substitute** | Trade goods and, better, **trade skills** (→ 18-02, → 18-03) |
| **Produce** | **Skills are the only thing you can produce indefinitely** (→ 23-05) |
| **Stage 4 needs** | Something people want that you can do again and again |
| **Verdict** | **The move from stock to skill happens here first** |
| **Where the numbers are** | → 19-01 · → 19-02 · → 18-02 · → 18-03 |

## The pattern, stated plainly

Read the verdict rows in order. Three things stand out:
1. **Water, light, soap and part of food can be solved where most people live.** Build those
   now.
2. **Fuel is stock-only, and firewood is hard to produce on a town lot.** For many
   households this row is the honest core of the case for a destination (→ 01-02, → 01-05).
3. **The class C medical rows have no stage 4 at all.** Nothing changes that. Preparation
   changes **how much time the stock buys** and **what you do with that time**.

## What to buy, in the order it pays off

| Item | What it moves forward | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Rain barrels and a downspout diverter | Water → stage 4 | The cheapest stage 4 step on this page |
| Spare filter elements | Water → stage 4 | A filter is useless once its element is |
| A good axe, saw, file and splitting maul | Fuel → stages 2 and 4 | → 16-06; only pays off with wood to cut |
| **Open-pollinated seed**, plenty | Food → stage 4 | → 05-03. Cheap, light and time-sensitive |
| A compost bin (or just a pile) | Soil → stage 4 | → 05-11 |
| Soap-making supplies | Hygiene → stage 4 | → 13-09 |
| Sewing kit, heavy needles, thread | Clothing → stage 2 | → 16-04 |
| **Next two sizes of children's clothing and boots**{{#if !has.child}} (if children may join you){{/if}} | Clothing → stage 2 | The clock nobody plans for |
| Traps and snare wire | Food → stage 3 | → 05-15 |
| Extra battery capacity | Power → stage 2 | → 09-05; the panel outlives the battery |

No money? Salvage. Every food-grade bucket, jug and barrel moves water forward. Scrap wood and
fallen wood are the only in-town fuel resupply (never treated wood indoors). Cloth in the
children's future sizes, files, blades, needles, thread and screws are small, light, and the
real limiting supply around every tool you own.

## When it runs out

This page is the "when it runs out" page for the whole binder.
- Work down the table and mark each row 1, 2, 3 or 4.
- **Any row still at stage 1 with a runway shorter than your plan is an unfunded debt.**
- **Fuel stays at stage 1 for almost every household.** That shapes the decision about where
  to be.
- **The class C rows never leave stage 1.** That sets the timeline.

## By phase

- **A, at home:** water, light, hygiene and part of food can reach stage 4 on most
  properties. Push everything reachable to stage 4 while the shops still work.
- **B, moving:** you carry stage 1 stock and stage 2 skills; **almost nothing produces while
  you travel.** Everything on this page is being used up during phase B, which is why phase B
  should be short (→ 01-03).
- **C, establishing:** the only phase where fuel, food and fat can reach stage 4 together, and
  only somewhere with land, timber and water. {{#if has.destinations}}Run every row of this
  table against each destination: {{#each destinations as x}}{{x.name}} ({{x.status_text}}; water: {{x.water_source_text}}); {{/each}}see → 01-05.{{else}}No destination is entered in settings; → 01-05 shows how to judge one against this table.{{/if}} A
  place where no one expects you is a possibility, not a plan: arrive self-sufficient.

pages.body:
# Skills that replace supplies

**What this page is for.** Everything else in this section is arithmetic on a shrinking pile.
A skill is different: it **does not run out, cannot be stolen, weighs nothing, travels with
you, and is worth more the longer things go on.** This page ranks the skills that actually end
a supply problem and says where in this binder to learn each one.

## Do this now

1. **Pick one skill from tier 1 below and do it this month**, badly, while a failure is funny
   rather than costly. Reading is not learning; the first try is always the worst.
2. **Every adult learns the water chain** (→ 03-04){{#if has.diabetes}} **and the diabetes
   routine** (→ 02-01, → 02-02, → 02-05, → 02-06){{/if}}{{#if has.anaphylaxis}} **and how to
   give epinephrine** (→ 02-03){{/if}}. If only one person knows a life-safety routine, the
   household depends on that one person being there.
3. **Put practice on the calendar** (→ 24-03). Skills fade. Unscheduled practice does not
   happen.
4. {{#if has.child}}**Teach the children the version that fits their age** (→ 20-04,
   → 20-07). Young children can fetch, sort and water plants: that is a real contribution, and
   it is how the skill outlives you. Which dangerous jobs children may do is a household
   worksheet: {{choice DC-24}} → 30-25{{else}}**Teach someone outside the household** one
   skill you know (→ 18-07). That is how a skill outlives you.{{/if}}

## What makes a skill worth learning

Rank a skill by four questions:
1. **Does it end a supply problem, or only stretch one?** Making soap ends one. Using less
   soap stretches one.
2. **How long until it is useful?** Water treatment: an afternoon. Gardening well: years.
3. **What does it still need?** A skill that depends on something irreplaceable is not a stage
   4 answer (→ 23-04). It is a substitute with extra steps.
4. **Is it worth something to other people?** Skills are the longest-lasting trade good there
   is (→ 18-03): you trade what you make and keep the ability.

## The ranking

**Tier 1: learn these first.** Biggest return, quickest to learn, matters for life and safety.

| Skill | What it replaces | Time to be competent | Where to learn it |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Water treatment**: settle, filter, boil or disinfect (EPA, Emergency Disinfection of Drinking Water) | Bottled water, and eventually the water utility | An afternoon to learn | → 03-04, → 03-08 |
| **Managing your household's medical conditions without the usual support**: storage without a fridge, what to do when a device fails, warning signs{{#if has.diabetes}} (diabetes: → 02-01, → 02-02, → 02-05, → 02-06){{/if}} | **Nothing. It does not replace the medicine**: it makes the supply last as it should and get used correctly | Weeks of deliberate practice | → 12-11 and your condition pages |
| **Cooking from raw ingredients**{{#if has.food_allergy}}, allergen-safe for your household's allergies{{/if}} | Packaged food{{#if has.food_allergy}} and dependence on labels (→ 02-04){{/if}} | Weeks | → 04-18, → 02-04 |
| **Fire: build it, control it, cook on it, put it out** | Grid cooking, and part of heating | A weekend, then a season of practice | → 06-01, → 07-01 |
| **First aid: bleeding, burns, wounds, spotting infection** | An emergency room you cannot reach | A course, then refreshers | → 12-01, → 12-02, → 12-03, → 12-04 |
| **Cooking on an open fire and in a Dutch oven** | The stove; also a big morale lift | A few weekends | → 07-01, → 07-04 |
| **Finding your way with a paper map and compass** | GPS and cell service | A weekend | → 01-03, → 25-04 |

**Tier 2: the multipliers.** Each ends a whole supply line for good.

| Skill | What it replaces | Time to be competent | Where to learn it |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Food preservation**: canning, drying, curing, fermenting | The freezer, and the store's shelf | A season each. **Canning follows tested process times** (National Center for Home Food Preservation): **Low-acid foods are pressure-canned to the published time and pressure, or not canned** (→ 30-01) | → 04-04, → 04-05, → 04-06, → 04-08 |
| **Gardening that actually yields** | Part of the food supply | **Years.** That is why you start now | → 05-01, → 05-02, → 05-11 |
| **Seed saving** | Buying seed: the difference between one garden and every garden after | A season, plus knowing what to plant | → 05-03 |
| **Soap making** | Soap, and with it most of the hygiene supply | A day to learn; **lye burns, so it needs care** | → 13-09 |
| **Sharpening and tool care** (OSHA, Hand and Power Tools) | New tools; good steel lasts decades | Hours to learn, years to master | → 16-02 |
| **Sewing and repair** | New clothing. This is the **permanent** clothing plan | Weeks | → 16-04, → 11-07 |
| **Butchering and rendering fat** | The butcher; fat also feeds lamps, soap and calories | A day with someone who knows how | → 05-09, → 10-04 |
| **Trapping and snaring** | Ammunition, and most of the effort of hunting | A season | → 05-15 |
| **Firearm cleaning and sighting-in**{{#if !has.firearms}} (only if you own or may come to own firearms){{/if}} | A gunsmith | A weekend | → 14-05, → 14-09, → 29-11 |

**Tier 3: deeper skills.** Long to learn, large payoff, mostly in phase C.

| Skill | What it replaces | Where to learn it |
|---|---|---|
| **Wood processing**: felling, cutting to length, splitting, seasoning | Bought fuel. **The phase C skill** | → 06-04, → 16-06 |
| **Small livestock**: chickens, rabbits | Bought protein and fat | → 05-04, → 05-05 |
| **Solar and electrical upkeep** | An electrician; keeps medical loads running | → 09-02, → 09-03 |
| **Radio operation** | The phone network | → 15-02, → 15-03 |
| **Basic building and weatherproofing** | A contractor; keeps a shelter warm | → 08-03, → 16-07 |
| **Basic metalwork** | Some hardware | → 16-08 |
| **Midwifery and advanced medical skills** | **Nothing. Know their limits** (→ 12-16) | → 12-12, → 02-12, → 12-16 |

## Skills nobody counts, and everybody needs

They are not on gear lists, and they carry more weight than half the tools in the garage.
- **Keeping a routine when nothing is normal** (→ 21-04): it keeps children steady and adults
  sane.
- **Calming a conflict** (→ 18-06, → 14-13): the cheapest security measure in this binder.
- **Teaching** (→ 18-07, → 20-03): how one person's skill becomes two people's.
- **Keeping records and an inventory** (→ 22-04): you cannot ration what you have not counted.
- **Saying no calmly** (→ 18-05, → 14-13): a real survival skill.
- **Sleeping properly** (→ 21-07): the multiplier under every other skill on this page.

## How to actually learn one

1. **Read the binder page once.** That is orientation, not ability.
2. **Do it with everything available**: shops, spare parts, someone to call.
3. **Do it again with one thing taken away**: no power, no running water, in the cold.
4. **Have someone else in the household do it while you watch and say nothing.**
5. **Write down what surprised you** on the page itself (→ 24-01).
6. **Repeat every year.** Everything here fades.

**Do not stockpile a tool for a skill you have never used.** An unused pressure canner, an
untested water filter and a gun that has never been sighted in are decorations. Every
purchase in this binder implies a practice session.

## What you need

| Item | Which skill | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Practice supplies (extra jars and lids, cheap practice ammunition if you shoot, seed, fabric scraps) | All of them | Cheap failure is the point |
| A wall calendar for practice | Scheduling | → 24-03 |
| **This binder, charged and installed**, plus any paper books you trust | All | Assume no internet: that is the whole premise |
| An in-person first-aid course | Medical | The one skill most worth paying an instructor for |
| A notebook for each skill | All | Your own notes beat any book, because they are about your own setup |

No money?
- **People.** A neighbour who cans, hunts, welds or gardens is worth more than any book, and
  the relationship is itself preparation (→ 18-01, → 18-03).
- **Libraries and university Extension offices**: free, local, reliable, and staffed by people
  whose job is to teach these skills (→ 25-03).
- **Old manuals and printed books** from thrift stores: the older ones already assume no
  internet.

## When it runs out

**It does not.** That is the point of this page.
- **Runway:** unlimited, but skills **fade** without practice. Budget one practice session a
  month; that is the real upkeep cost.
- **Ration:** never ration teaching. A skill known by one person is a supply line with one
  truck.
- **Resupply:** teach it. Two people knowing it costs nothing and doubles it.
- **Substitute:** a skill **is** the substitute. Its only replacement is someone else's skill,
  which costs you trade.
- **The exception, once more:** no skill produces insulin, epinephrine, infant formula or most
  daily prescriptions. Skills change how far the stock goes and how well you use the time it
  buys. They do not change how those rows end (→ 23-04).

## By phase

- **A, at home:** the learning phase. Every skill here is cheaper, safer and faster to learn
  now, with the hardware store open and a failed batch costing nothing but groceries.
- **B, moving:** you carry only what you know. Fire, water, finding your way, first aid, and
  keeping everyone fed and calm are the skills that travel.
- **C, establishing:** wood, food production, livestock and building come to the front; the
  tier 3 skills finally have the room and the reason to pay off.

# Skills to practise now

**What this section holds.** 4 pages in this build. Pages marked FOR YOU matter most for your household and come first.

- → 24-01 **Skills checklist and practice schedule**: A list of the skills this binder relies on, a way to score each adult honestly, and a schedule for practising.
- → 24-02 **Family drills: fire, grab-and-go, shelter, medical, blackout**: Under stress, people do what they have practised, not what they have read.
- → 24-03 **Seasonal practice plan**: Most preparedness skills have a season.
- → 24-04 **Running a blackout weekend**: The most valuable exercise in this binder.

pages.body:
# Skills checklist and practice schedule

**What this page is for.** A list of the skills this binder relies on, a way to score each
adult honestly, and a schedule for practising. Practise **while failure is free**: with the
shops open, emergency care a phone call away and a hardware store to fix your mistake.

> **Caution.** Two practice rules have no exceptions. **Anything that burns fuel is practised
> with a working carbon monoxide alarm and fresh air** (→ 08-02): **Never run a generator,
> charcoal, or any engine indoors, in a garage, or near an open window.** And **medical
> fallbacks** (a pump failing, a missed dose) **are practised with your clinician's
> instructions, not from a checklist** (→ 12-11).

## Do this now

1. **Score each adult honestly** on the checklist below, 0 to 3. Most people score 1 on things
   they believe they can do, because reading is not doing.
2. **Pick the three lowest scores marked ★** and schedule them this quarter. Three real skills a
   quarter is twelve a year, which is most of this list.
3. **Score every adult separately.** A skill only one person has fails when that person is
   away, hurt or asleep (→ 18-07).
4. **Write the date on every line you practise.** An undated tick is a memory, not a record.

Adults in your household (one column each below; add columns by hand if you need more):
{{#each adults as a}}**{{a.label}}** · {{else}}______ · ______{{/each}}

## The scoring scale

| Score | Meaning | The honest test |
|---|---|---|
| **0** | Never done it | You have read about it |
| **1** | Done once, with help and everything to hand | You would need to look it up |
| **2** | Done alone, in good conditions | You could do it today, slowly |
| **3** | Done alone **in bad conditions**: dark, cold, tired, no internet | You could teach it |

**Only a 3 counts in a plan.** A 2 is a skill you have; a 3 is a skill you can rely on when it
is cold, dark and a child is crying. Making conditions worse on purpose is the whole practice
method.

### The five-step method (from → 23-05)

1. Read the page. 2. Do it with everything available. 3. **Do it with one thing taken away**:
no power, no running water, in the cold, in the dark, one-handed. 4. **Have someone else do it
while you say nothing.** 5. **Write what surprised you on the page.** Your notes about your own
stove, your own water heater and your own pump are worth more than any source this binder
cites.

### How fast skills fade, and how often to practise

| Fades | Skills | Practise again (our suggestion) |
|---|---|---|
| **Fast** | Anything done under stress: bleeding control, epinephrine, the grab-and-go, medical device fallbacks | **Every 3 to 6 months** |
| **Medium** | Fire in bad weather, cooking on coals, map and compass, radio, sharpening | **Every year** |
| **Slow** | Gardening, canning, sewing, soap, butchering | **Each season it applies** |
| **Hardly** | Knots, knowing the plan | At the yearly review (→ 25-10) |

The intervals are this binder's suggestion, not a published standard; a course you take may set its
own. **The fast list is also the life-safety list.** That is why → 24-02 exists.

## The checklist

Score 0 to 3 for each adult and note the date. **★ = do this one first.** Rows without a ★
for your household still matter; they are just not first.

### A. Life safety (fast fade: drill these)

| ★ | Skill | A1 | A2 | A3 | Last done | Page |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| {{#if has.epinephrine}}★{{/if}} | **Use an epinephrine auto-injector** (practise with a trainer device, never a live one) and say the person's emergency plan aloud | | | | | → 02-03 |
| {{#if has.anaphylaxis}}★{{/if}} | **Recognise anaphylaxis** and act in under a minute | | | | | → 02-03 |
| {{#if has.condition.CL-02}}★{{/if}} | **Pump-to-injection fallback**, start to finish, as your clinician wrote it | | | | | → 02-02 |
| {{#if has.diabetes}}★{{/if}} | **Recognise and act on low and high blood sugar and diabetic ketoacidosis** | | | | | → 02-01, → 02-05 |
| ★ | **Use a tourniquet and pack a wound** (a Stop the Bleed course). **Never loosen a tourniquet once placed while help can still come; mark the time. If no help will ever come, the conversion decision is DC-25 (→ 30-26).** | | | | | → 12-02 |
| ★ | **Recognise hypothermia and frostbite**, and rewarm correctly | | | | | → 08-05 |
| ★ | **Test the carbon monoxide alarms, and know what to do when one sounds**: everyone out, then call | | | | | → 08-02 |
| ★ | **The grab-and-go**: people{{#if has.pets}}, pets{{/if}}, medical kit, bags, out | | | | | → 22-03 |
| | Use a fire extinguisher (→ 29-12); shut off gas, water and power | | | | | → 16-12, → 29-04 |
| {{#if has.child}}★{{/if}} | CPR and choking response{{#if has.infant}}, including infant{{/if}} (take the class) | | | | | → 12-18 |
| {{#if has.condition.CL-11}}★{{/if}} | Seizure first aid | | | | | → 02-11 |

### B. Water

| ★ | Skill | A1 | A2 | A3 | Last done | Page |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ★ | **Filter, treat, store**: the full chain, alone (EPA, Emergency Disinfection of Drinking Water) | | | | | → 03-04 |
| ★ | **Measure bleach correctly** for a known volume of water, from the label's strength | | | | | → 03-04, → 29-05 |
| | **Make a pool-shock stock solution** by the two-step method only (granules never go straight into drinking water), outdoors, eye protection on. **Bleach or pool shock is never mixed with ammonia, acids or other cleaners.** | | | | | → 03-04 |
| | Boil and cool water safely outdoors | | | | | → 07-01 |
| {{#if has.pool}}★{{/if}} | **Distil pool or salty water** and taste the result | | | | | → 03-03 |
| {{#if is.snow_region}}★{{/if}} | Melt snow for water efficiently (the fuel it takes is the lesson) | | | | | → 03-06 |
| | Set up and clear rain catchment; screen it | | | | | → 03-05 |
| | Shut off and drain the house water; get water out of the water heater | | | | | → 03-02 |
| {{#if has.well}}★{{/if}} | **Draw water from a well with a bailer** (on a well you are allowed to use) | | | | | → 03-10 |

### C. Fire, heat, cooking

| ★ | Skill | A1 | A2 | A3 | Last done | Page |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ★ | **Fire in wind, rain or snow**, with cold hands | | | | | → 06-01 |
| ★ | **Cook a full family meal outdoors** on fire or a camp stove | | | | | → 07-01, → 07-05 |
| | Fire with a ferro rod only, no lighter | | | | | → 06-01 |
| {{#if has.wood_stove}}★{{/if}} | Bank a fire overnight and bring it back in the morning | | | | | → 06-02, → 08-08 |
| | Bake in a Dutch oven on coals | | | | | → 07-04 |
| | Build and cook on a rocket stove | | | | | → 07-02 |
| | Solar cooking, start to finish | | | | | → 07-03 |
| | Split and stack wood; note how long it took you | | | | | → 06-03 |
| {{#if has.kerosene_heater}}★{{/if}} | **Wick kerosene heater**: light it, run it 30 minutes, let it cool, refuel **outdoors** from a labelled kerosene can, shut it down. Read the can's label aloud and smell before pouring. **Fuel is never stored or transferred near an open flame or a running appliance.** | | | | | → 08-10, → 06-06 |
| {{#if has.propane_heater}}★{{/if}} | **Portable propane heater**: connect, leak-test with soapy water, light and shut down as the manual says; cylinder valve closed first | | | | | → 08-09 |
| ★ | **Put up and test every carbon monoxide alarm** ({{ gear.co_alarms }} in settings) **before the first fuel-burning heater is lit**: one where people sleep, one on each level | | | | | → 08-02 |
| {{#if has.unvented_heater}}★{{/if}} | Set up the one-room heating plan for real, for a night, in the warm room. Whether a heater runs while people sleep is a household choice: {{choice DC-01}} → 30-02 | | | | | → 08-01 |

### D. Food

| ★ | Skill | A1 | A2 | A3 | Last done | Page |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ★ | **Cook a week of meals from the pantry alone**, no shopping | | | | | → 04-18 |
| {{#if has.food_allergy}}★{{/if}} | **Cook allergen-safe from raw ingredients** for the household's allergies | | | | | → 02-04 |
| {{#if has.infant}}★{{/if}} | Prepare infant feeding safely with no running water | | | | | → 20-05 |
| | Water-bath can a tested recipe (National Center for Home Food Preservation) | | | | | → 04-04 |
| {{#if has.pressure_canner}}★{{/if}} | Pressure can a tested recipe (have the gauge checked) | | | | | → 04-05 |
| | Dry and rehydrate something you would actually eat | | | | | → 04-06 |
| | Ferment (sauerkraut is the beginner's) | | | | | → 04-08 |
| | Sprout a jar in winter | | | | | → 04-16 |
| | Pack staples in sealed bags with oxygen absorbers | | | | | → 04-03 |
| | Grow a bed from seed to harvest; save seed from it | | | | | → 05-01, → 05-03 |
| | Set and check a trap line legally, in season | | | | | → 05-15 |
| | Field dress and butcher an animal | | | | | → 05-09 |
| {{#if is.cold_winters}}★{{/if}} | Fish{{#if is.cold_winters}}, including through ice with its safety margin{{/if}} | | | | | → 05-08 |

### E. Power and light

| ★ | Skill | A1 | A2 | A3 | Last done | Page |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| {{#if has.refrigerated_meds}}★{{else}}{{#if has.cpap}}★{{else}}{{#if has.oxygen}}★{{/if}}{{/if}}{{/if}} | **Run the medical devices and medicine cooling for 72 hours off-grid**, measured | | | | | → 09-10, → 09-06 |
| {{#if has.refrigerated_meds}}★{{/if}} | **Set up the medicine cooler from its box** on battery power, thermometer inside, and check it holds the label's temperature over 24 hours | | | | | → 09-10, → 29-07 |
| | Set up panel, controller and battery, and read the numbers | | | | | → 09-09 |
| | Charge from the vehicle safely (engine running outdoors only) | | | | | → 09-11 |
| {{#if has.generator}}★{{/if}} | **Generator first start and refuel**: outdoors, at least 20 feet from the house, exhaust away, oil checked first, cool before refuelling (→ 09-04, → 09-15). **Never connect a generator to house wiring except through a transfer switch, or an interlock kit with the main breaker off.** | | | | | → 09-04 |
| {{#if has.power_station}}★{{/if}} | Run a power station through a full day; read its screen as the truth, not your estimate | | | | | → 09-03, → 09-16 |
| {{#if has.solar}}★{{/if}} | Connect your own panels to your own station within the station's input limits (→ 28-07) | | | | | → 09-02, → 28-01 |
| | Wire a 12-volt circuit; use a multimeter; fuse it | | | | | → 09-08 |
| | Make an oil lamp and a candle that work | | | | | → 10-03, → 10-04 |

### F. Medical (beyond section A)

| ★ | Skill | A1 | A2 | A3 | Last done | Page |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| | Clean, close and dress a wound; recognise infection | | | | | → 12-14, → 12-04 |
| | Mix and give oral rehydration solution | | | | | → 12-05 |
| | Splint a limb with what is in the room | | | | | → 12-09 |
| | Treat a burn correctly | | | | | → 12-03 |
| | Take temperature, pulse and breathing rate{{#if has.child}} on a child{{/if}} | | | | | → 12-05 |
| | Dental first aid: a temporary filling | | | | | → 12-06, → 12-20 |

### G. Sanitation, hygiene, clothing

| ★ | Skill | A1 | A2 | A3 | Last done | Page |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ★ | **Run the bucket toilet for a weekend**, including disposal | | | | | → 13-01 |
| | Hand-wash and dry a load of laundry{{#if is.cold_winters}} in winter{{/if}} | | | | | → 13-04 |
| | Make soap | | | | | → 13-09 |
| | Wash dishes safely with little water | | | | | → 13-10 |
| | Site and dig a latrine correctly | | | | | → 13-07 |
| | Dress in layers for your coldest normal week (January mean low here: {{ region.home.jan_low_f }} °F) and stay dry while working | | | | | → 11-01, → 11-03 |
| | Repair a garment; patch a boot | | | | | → 11-07, → 16-04 |

### H. Tools, repair, transport

| ★ | Skill | A1 | A2 | A3 | Last done | Page |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ★ | **Sharpen a knife and an axe** until they shave | | | | | → 16-02 |
| | Fell, cut up and split safely | | | | | → 16-06 |
| | Five knots by feel: bowline, taut-line hitch, trucker's hitch, clove hitch, square knot | | | | | → 16-03 |
| | Patch a roof or window with tarp and tape in bad weather | | | | | → 16-05 |
| | Fix a bicycle: tube, chain, brake | | | | | → 16-09 |
| | Drill and saw accurately by hand | | | | | → 16-01 |
| {{#if has.trailer}}★{{/if}} | **Back the trailer** in an empty lot **before the first loaded trip**; hitch up and check the lights alone; feel each hub at every stop | | | | | → 16-11 |
| {{#if has.vehicle}}★{{/if}} | Change a tire and deal with a flat on the roadside | | | | | → 16-10 |
| | **Load fuel for a trip**: cans upright, strapped, outside the passenger space where possible. Carrying it inside: {{choice DC-06}} → 30-07 | | | | | → 06-08 |
| | **Transfer fuel** from can to tank **outdoors**, engine off and cool, label read aloud and smelled first | | | | | → 06-07, → 06-06 |

### I. Security and communications

| ★ | Skill | A1 | A2 | A3 | Last done | Page |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| {{#if has.firearms}}★{{/if}} | **Clear, field-strip, clean and reassemble each firearm** (→ 29-11) | | | | | → 14-05 |
| {{#if has.firearms}}★{{/if}} | **Confirm the sights at known distances.** Where you may shoot is a household choice: {{choice DC-11}} → 30-12 | | | | | → 14-09 |
| {{#if has.firearms}}★{{/if}} | **Dry practice by the rules on → 14-15**: checked three times, a set place, no ammunition in the room | | | | | → 14-15 |
| | Replace springs and small parts from spares | | | | | → 14-06 |
| {{#if has.noaa_radio}}★{{/if}} | Run the NOAA Weather Radio and program your SAME code (→ 29-09) | | | | | → 15-01 |
| {{#if has.gmrs}}★{{/if}} | Use the handheld radios; run the family check-in schedule | | | | | → 15-02, → 15-03 |
| {{#if has.ham}}★{{/if}} | Put up a wire antenna and make a contact | | | | | → 15-06 |
| | Follow a route with a paper map and compass | | | | | → 25-04 |
| | Calm a confrontation (role-play it) | | | | | → 14-13 |

### J. Family and household

| ★ | Skill | A1 | A2 | A3 | Last done | Page |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| {{#if has.child}}★{{/if}} | **Every child knows the plan** at their level{{#if has.child}}: {{#each children as c}}{{c.label}} ({{c.age_text}}). {{/each}}{{else}}. {{/if}}Which jobs each child may do: {{choice DC-24}} → 30-25 | | | | | → 20-04 |
| ★ | **Complete the inventory** and work out the runways | | | | | → 22-04, → 23-02 |
| {{#if has.child}}★{{/if}} | Run a school day with no screens | | | | | → 20-03 |
| | Keep the routine through a blackout weekend | | | | | → 24-04, → 21-04 |
| {{#if has.pets}}★{{/if}} | Look after the pets through a disruption | | | | | → 20-09 |
| | Trade something real with a neighbour | | | | | → 18-02 |

## The practice schedule

| How often | What | Where |
|---|---|---|
| **Monthly** | One skill from the lowest-scoring ★ rows | This page |
| **Quarterly** | One family drill | → 24-02 |
| **Twice a year** | Kit checks, expiry dates{{#if has.child}}, children's sizes{{/if}}, inventory | → 22-03, → 22-04 |
| **Twice a year** | **A blackout weekend** | → 24-04 |
| **Each season** | That season's skills: garden, preserving, wood, winter | → 24-03 |
| **Yearly** | Re-score this whole page; update the binder | → 25-10 |

## What you need

{{#if has.epinephrine}}An **epinephrine trainer device** (no needle, no drug), {{/if}}a Stop the
Bleed kit and course, practice supplies (extra jars and lids, seed, fabric scraps, a cheap knife
to learn sharpening on{{#if has.firearms}}, inexpensive practice ammunition{{/if}}), a wall
calendar and a notebook for each skill. **Practice supplies are the cheapest line on → 22-07
and the one most often skipped.**

No money? Scrap wood, thrift-store clothing to practise repairs on, a borrowed tool, and best of
all **a neighbour who already knows how** (→ 18-03). An hour watching someone skilled beats a
week of reading.

## When it runs out

Skills do not run out; **chances to practise do.** Once the grid is down, every practice
session costs real supplies and real risk, and mistakes stop being free.
- **Runway:** exactly as long as normal life lasts.
- **Ration:** do not. Practice is the cheapest thing in this binder.
- **Resupply:** teach someone. Teaching is the form of practice that sticks best (→ 18-07).
- **Substitute:** none. A skill you have only read about is a plan, not an ability.

## By phase

- **A, at home:** all of it. This is when practice is free.
- **B, moving:** only the ★ rows matter: medical, fire, water, warmth, finding your way, the
  grab-and-go.
- **C, establishing:** the slow-fade production skills come to the front; keep drilling the ★
  rows anyway.

pages.body:
# Family drills: fire, grab-and-go, shelter, medical, blackout

**What this page is for.** Under stress, people do what they have practised, not what they
have read. These drills take ten minutes each, four times a year, and they find the problems
(a blocked exit, a missing battery, a bag nobody can lift) while finding them costs nothing.

> **Caution: how you run a drill matters as much as running it.** {{#if has.child}}With
> children in the house, **a frightening drill is a failed drill**: a child scared of the
> practice may freeze in the real thing. Keep it short, calm, matter-of-fact and praised.
> {{/if}}**Never use a live epinephrine auto-injector in a drill**: trainer devices only.
> **Never run a fuel-burning drill without a working carbon monoxide alarm** (→ 08-02).
> **Never run a generator, charcoal, or any engine indoors, in a garage, or near an open
> window.**

## Do this now

1. **Run the fire-and-exit drill this month.** A house fire is the life-threatening emergency
   your household is most likely to actually face. Ready.gov says a fire can become
   life-threatening in two minutes (Ready.gov, Home Fires).
2. **Run the grab-and-go drill** (→ 22-03), timed, and write the time down. The first time is
   always embarrassing. That is the point.
3. **Put the four quarterly drills on the calendar**: one a quarter, ten minutes each.
4. {{#if has.child}}**Teach each child who can talk three things by heart**: their full name
   and their grown-ups' names; what the smoke alarm sounds like and where to meet; and **"if
   you feel funny or hurt, tell a grown-up right away."**{{else}}**Agree who checks on whom**
   (neighbours, relatives nearby) and add them to the comms plan (→ 15-03).{{/if}}

## Drill rules: read before running any of them

1. **Announce the first run.** Surprise drills are for people who have done the announced
   version. Ambushing small children teaches fear, not what to do.
2. **Keep it under ten minutes.** Long drills get resisted, and resisted drills stop happening.
3. **Time it, write it down, try to beat it.** A stopwatch works better than a lecture.
4. **Praise taking part; never criticise the performance.** Name the specific thing someone
   did well (CDC, Positive Parenting Tips).
5. **Debrief for five minutes**: what worked, what did not, what to change (below).
6. **Rotate who leads.** Every adult must be able to run the whole thing.{{#if has.child}}
   Older children can be "in charge" of one step.{{/if}}
7. **Make one thing harder each repeat**: in the dark, a phone "dead", one adult missing, in
   winter clothing.
8. **Stop if a child is truly frightened**, finish gently, and try a smaller version next time
   (→ 20-08).

## Who needs what in a drill

Your household, from settings:
{{#each members as m}}- **{{m.label}}** ({{m.role}}, {{m.age_text}}): job in the drill ______________ · who helps them ______________
{{/each}}

{{#if has.infant}}- **Babies are carried, always.** Decide now which adult takes which baby, so no
  one has to think about it at 2 a.m. The drill is that the adults never hesitate.
{{/if}}{{#if has.young_child}}- **Children under 6** need an adult assigned to them by name. Give them a small job
  (carry the flashlight, blow the whistle at the meeting point): a job is the best thing a young
  child has against fear (→ 20-07, → 20-08).
{{/if}}{{#if has.teen}}- **Teenagers** can lead a step, carry a bag, and take a younger child. Practise
  them doing it with no adult nearby.
{{/if}}{{#if has.elder}}- **Older adults**: plan for slower stairs, hearing aids and glasses at the bedside,
  and medicines in the grab (Ready.gov, Older Adults).
{{/if}}{{#if has.mobility_aid}}- **Someone uses a wheelchair or walker**: walk every route with the chair or walker,
  not on foot; know which exits it fits through and who helps (Ready.gov, Individuals with
  Disabilities).
{{/if}}{{#if has.pets}}- **Pets**: carriers and leashes stay where they can be reached, not behind boxes.
  **Never go back into a burning building for a pet.**
{{/if}}

## Drill 1: fire and exit (quarterly; the most important one)

**Scenario:** the smoke alarm sounds at night.

| Step | Who | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Everyone | **Sound the real alarm** (its test button) so everyone knows the noise |
| 2 | Adults | One adult to each person who needs help{{#if has.infant}}; **babies are carried**{{/if}} |
| 3 | Everyone | Out **by the main route**; then run it again with that route blocked |
| 4 | Everyone | **Meet at one fixed outside spot**, touch it and stay. Same spot every time: ______________ |
| 5 | Adults | Head count{{#if has.pets}}, pets only if it is safe; **never go back in for a pet**{{/if}} |
| 6 | Everyone | Debrief: what was in the way, what was dark, what was hard |

{{photo meeting-point}}

**Teach it and mean it: get out, stay out.** Practise crawling low under smoke, feeling a door
with the back of your hand before opening it, and the meeting point. Ready.gov advises practising
your escape plan at least twice a year and having two ways out of every room (Ready.gov, Home
Fires). **Upstairs window exits and escape ladders** get their own, separate practice: walk it
slowly, do not rush it (→ 20-02).

## Drill 2: the grab-and-go (quarterly)

**Scenario:** you have one minute to leave.
- **Timed.** People{{#if has.pets}}, pets{{/if}}, **medical kit**{{#if has.refrigerated_meds}} and the medicine cooler{{/if}}, go-bags, phones, keys, wallets,
  out the door (→ 22-03).
- **Run it in the dark** the second time. Then with one adult "unavailable".
- **What it always finds:** bags moved, a broken strap, carriers buried in storage, and nobody
  sure who takes which child.
- **Then run the 10-minute version**: documents, water, food box, coats and boots for
  {{ household.size }}. Is the pile really ready where it should be (→ 22-05)?

## Drill 3: storm shelter (before your storm season; quarterly in season)

**Scenario:** a tornado warning for your area, or a severe storm warning.

NWS advice: get to the **lowest floor, the most interior room with no windows**, and **cover
your head** (NWS, Tornado Safety; → 17-02, → 17-06). Your spot:
{{#if has.mobile_home}}- **You live in a mobile or manufactured home. It is not a safe shelter in a tornado,
  even tied down.** NOAA's Storm Prediction Center says leave it for a sturdy building or a
  storm shelter **before** the storm arrives (NOAA SPC, Tornado Safety FAQ). Your drill is
  the drive or walk to that building: where it is ______________, how long it takes ______.
{{/if}}{{#if has.basement}}- **Basement**, under something sturdy, away from windows{{#if has.walkout}} and away from the walkout's glass wall{{/if}}.
{{/if}}{{#if has.shelter_room}}- **Your named interior room**: {{ dwelling.shelter_room }}.
{{/if}}{{#if has.apartment}}- **Apartment**: an interior hallway or bathroom on the lowest floor you can reach
  safely; not the top floor. Know the stairs; never the elevator.
{{/if}}- Shelter spot in writing: ______________. Second choice if the first smells of gas or is
  blocked: ______________.

{{photo shelter-spot}}

- **Practise getting everyone there**{{#if has.child}}, carrying the small children{{/if}}{{#if has.mobility_aid}} and moving the person who uses a wheelchair or walker{{/if}}, shoes on, the weather radio going (→ 15-01).
  Helmets (bike helmets are fine) protect heads.
- **Keep at the shelter spot:** shoes for everyone, a light, a whistle, water, a weather radio.
- **Medicines that must stay in a temperature range are grabbed on the way, not stored in the
  shelter.** An unheated basement or storm room can freeze or overheat them (→ 29-07).
  {{#if has.epinephrine}}Epinephrine travels with the person or the medical kit.{{/if}}
- **The debrief question:** how long did it take, and would that have been fast enough at 2 a.m.?

## Drill 4: medical drills (quarterly; rotate them)

These are fast-fade skills (→ 24-01). Run one each quarter.

**4a. Severe allergic reaction (anaphylaxis).**{{#if has.anaphylaxis}} Someone in your household has an anaphylaxis allergy (→ 02-03).{{/if}}
- **Read the person's written emergency plan aloud**, then have another adult do it.
- **Practise with a trainer auto-injector** on the correct spot (the outer thigh), saying it
  aloud: *epinephrine first, then call for help, then a second dose if the plan says so*
  (CDC, Recognizing and Responding to Anaphylaxis).
- **Practise finding it in the dark** in every place it is kept: the person's bag, the other
  adults' bags, the vehicles, the house kit.
- Rehearse the babysitter or grandparent version: **someone who has never done this must be
  able to follow the plan.**

**4b. Diabetes emergency.**{{#if has.diabetes}} Someone in your household has diabetes (→ 02-01, → 02-05).{{/if}}
- **Severe low blood sugar:** the other adults find the emergency glucagon and **go through the
  steps on a trainer or the package diagram**, not just point at the box; say the signs aloud
  and where the fast sugar is kept.
- **Pump or sensor failure:** walk through the backup plan your clinician wrote, out loud
  (→ 02-02).
- **Power loss:** run the devices and phone on a power bank and check the runtime you believe
  (→ 09-10).
- **Heat and cold:** practise where the insulin goes on a very cold car trip and a very hot one
  (→ 29-07). **A frozen-then-thawed insulin vial or pen is discarded.**
{{#if has.child}}- **Children's version:** if a grown-up collapses, the child's job is noise and feet (shout,
  whistle, run for help), never medicine (→ 20-04).
{{/if}}

**4c. Bleeding.**
- Tourniquet on a limb (a practice device), wound packing on a trainer, and **saying the time
  aloud and writing it down**. **Never loosen a tourniquet once placed while help can still
  come; mark the time. If no help will ever come, the conversion decision is DC-25 (→ 30-26).**
  (→ 12-02)

**4d. Your household's own condition.**
{{#if has.oxygen}}- Oxygen: switch from concentrator to cylinder in the dark; read the cylinder gauge (→ 02-08).
{{/if}}{{#if has.cpap}}- CPAP: run it for a night on battery and note the percentage left in the morning (→ 02-24, → 09-10).
{{/if}}{{#if has.condition.CL-11}}- Seizure: every adult says the seizure first-aid steps aloud and times a pretend seizure (→ 02-11).
{{/if}}- Other: ______________ (from the condition page's warning signs, → 12-11).

## Drill 5: communications (twice a year)

- **Everyone finds the printed contact card** and reads out the out-of-area contact
  ({{ contacts.out_of_area.name }}) and the meeting points (→ 15-03).
{{#if has.gmrs}}- **Handheld radios:** everyone can switch one on, find the family channel and pass a
  message (→ 15-02).
{{/if}}{{#if has.noaa_radio}}- **NOAA Weather Radio:** anyone can switch it on and get the local forecast (→ 15-01).
{{/if}}- **The "phones are dead" version:** how do you find each other with no phones and no power?
  If there is no answer, that is the finding. Fix it on → 15-03.

## Drill 6: blackout (twice a year; see → 24-04)

The full version is a whole weekend with the main breaker off (→ 24-04). **The half version** is
one evening with the power off: cook a meal, light the house, do bedtime, and write down every
single thing you reached for that did not work.

## Drill 7: the sky call (once each season)

**Scenario:** there is no forecast; you are the forecast.
- **Write tomorrow's weather call down**: sky, wind, pressure trend if you have a barometer,
  your prediction. **Before** checking the weather radio (→ 17-10, → 15-01).
- Check it, and **score it right or wrong on the page.** No partial credit.
- One call a season keeps the skill alive while a real forecast still exists to grade you.

## Drill 8: heat and generator (every year, before {{#if is.cold_winters}}the first hard freeze{{else}}the season you would need them{{/if}})

**Scenario:** the power is out in bad weather and nobody in the house has ever lit the heater
or started the generator. **This drill exists so the first time is not that night.**
**Every adult at the gear**, in daylight and calm weather.{{#if has.child}} **Children with
another adult or away: never within reach of a lit heater, open fuel or a running
generator.**{{/if}} A fire extinguisher within reach (→ 29-12). The manuals and the full pages
govern every step.

**8a. Carbon monoxide alarms (do this first; 10 minutes).**
- Find the alarms ({{ gear.co_alarms }} CO and {{ gear.smoke_alarms }} smoke in settings).
  **Confirm they run on batteries**: an alarm that only plugs in does nothing in an outage.
- Put batteries in and hold **TEST** until each sounds. Mark the mounting spots: one where
  people sleep (in the warm room, → 08-01), one on every level, not in a dead-air corner and not
  right next to a heater (→ 08-02). Buy to that number.
- Mount them now, or store them **with batteries** beside the heater so they can be up in two
  minutes.

{{#if has.kerosene_heater}}**8b. Wick kerosene heater practice light** (first time about 2 hours, mostly waiting; → 08-10).
- Unbox, assemble, batteries in. **Fill outdoors** from a **labelled kerosene can**; read the
  label aloud first. **Fuel is never stored or transferred near an open flame or a running
  appliance.**
- Let the new wick soak as long as the manual says before lighting. Lighting early ruins it.
- **First burn outdoors** (factory oils burn off), never in a garage. Check the flame height
  the manual gives.
- Shut down as the manual says, confirm the flame is out, and wait before any relight. When
  cool, test the tip-over shut-off.
{{/if}}{{#if has.propane_heater}}**8c. Portable propane heater practice light** (30 minutes; → 08-09).
- Outdoors, or for the full rehearsal in the warm room with the CO alarm up and the fresh-air
  openings the manual requires.
- Connect as the manual says; **soapy-water leak test** at every joint. Light, hold, and
  confirm the flame.
- Shut down: **cylinder valve closed first**, let the line burn empty, then the control to off.
- Where the cylinder sits: {{choice DC-02}} → 30-03
{{/if}}{{#if has.generator}}**8d. Generator first start** (about 1 hour; → 09-04, → 09-15).
- **Outdoors only, at least 20 feet from the house, exhaust pointed away** (CDC, Carbon Monoxide
  Poisoning: Basics). Never in a garage, even with the door open. A CO alarm on inside, on the
  generator side of the house.
- Follow the manual's first-start steps in order: **oil first**, fuel, start, a light load.
  Prove one real job: charge a power station or run one appliance through an outdoor-rated cord.
- **Never connect a generator to house wiring except through a transfer switch, or an interlock
  kit with the main breaker off. Never backfeed through an outlet with a double-male ("suicide")
  cord.**
- Shut down, let it cool before refuelling, log the date and hours run.
{{/if}}
Running an unvented heater while people sleep is a household choice: {{choice DC-01}} → 30-02

**What drill 8 always finds:** a missing battery, no soapy-water bottle, a hose or cord that
does not reach, a fuel can nobody labelled. Fix it before you need it.

## Practice for children (make it a game)

| Age | What they practise | How it is framed |
|---|---|---|
| **Under 2** | Nothing: they are carried | The drill is that the adults never hesitate about who takes them |
| **2 to 5** | Their name and a grown-up's name; the meeting spot; "tell a grown-up right away if you feel funny"; stop, drop and roll; blowing a whistle; one small job | **A game with a stopwatch and a high five** |
| **6 to 12** | All of the above, plus: the home address, the out-of-area contact's name, feeling a door before opening it, the shelter spot | Give them a real step to lead |
| **13 to 17** | Everything the adults do, except jobs your household has ruled out | Practise them leading a younger child |

Your children: {{#each children as c}}**{{c.label}}** ({{c.age_text}}) · {{else}}none listed · {{/each}}{{#each teens as t}}**{{t.label}}** ({{t.age_text}}) · {{/each}}
Which risky jobs each child may help with: {{choice DC-24}} → 30-25

## The debrief: where the value is

Five minutes, every time, three questions:
1. **What took longer than we expected?**
2. **What did we reach for that was not there or did not work?**
3. **What one thing do we change: in the house, in a kit, or in this binder?**

Write the change on the page it affects. **A drill that changes nothing was a performance.**

## Targets: write the result against a number

Timing is half the record; the other half is a target. **Set your own targets in pencil** and
tighten them as real times come in. Never tighten one by shaming a slow run.

| Drill | Our target | Our result |
|---|---|---|
| Grab-and-go | Out the door in ______ seconds | ______ |
| Fire and exit | Everyone out and at the meeting spot in ______ minutes (a fire can become life-threatening in two, Ready.gov) | ______ |
| Shelter | Everyone at the shelter spot in ______ minutes | ______ |
| Anaphylaxis | Plan recited without errors; trainer on the right spot | ______ |
| Sky call | Right ______ out of 4 this year | ______ |
| CO alarms | Every alarm sounds on TEST; battery-powered; spots marked | ______ |
| Heaters | Each lit, held and shut down by **each** adult without the page; no leak bubbles | ______ |
| Generator | Started, ran a real load, shut down and logged. Date: ______ | ______ |

## The yearly drill log

```
DATE       DRILL                 TIME/RESULT     WHAT WE CHANGED
________   ____________________  ____________    ______________________________
________   ____________________  ____________    ______________________________
________   ____________________  ____________    ______________________________
________   ____________________  ____________    ______________________________
```

## What you need

{{#if has.epinephrine}}An **epinephrine trainer device** (ask the prescriber or the maker; they
are often free), {{/if}}a tourniquet and wound-packing trainer, a stopwatch or phone timer,
whistles for everyone, helmets for the shelter spot, working smoke and CO alarms with fresh
batteries, and escape ladders for upstairs bedrooms.

No money? Drills cost nothing but time. A rolled towel practises wound packing; a kitchen timer
times the grab. **The only thing with no substitute is the trainer auto-injector**: never
practise with a live one.

## When it runs out

Drills do not run out; **the willingness to run them does.**
- **Runway:** enthusiasm lasts about two drills. Then it becomes a calendar item or it stops.
- **Ration:** short and often beats long and rare. Ten minutes, four times a year.
- **Resupply:** let a child lead one; let them "catch" the adults out.
- **Substitute:** none. A plan nobody has rehearsed is a document, not a plan.

## By phase

- **A, at home:** every drill here, on a calendar, for good. Most of them cover emergencies
  that happen in normal life too: fire, storms, a severe allergic reaction, a winter outage.
- **B, moving:** the grab and comms drills **are** the phase B plan. Add a "reload the vehicle
  at a stop" drill and a "one adult alone with all the children" version.
- **C, establishing:** run all of them again at the new place in the first week. New building,
  new exits, new meeting spot, new shelter spot: the old drills are wrong there.

pages.body:
# Seasonal practice plan

**What this page is for.** Most preparedness skills have a season. You cannot practise
cold-weather cooking in July or can tomatoes in March, and **wood you cut this autumn is not
fuel until next year.** This is a year-round calendar that puts each skill in the month where
it belongs, adjusted to where you live.

**Your home base:** {{ region.home.county }}, {{ region.home.state_name }} · hardiness zone
{{ region.home.zone }} · median last spring frost {{ region.home.last_frost }} · median first
fall frost {{ region.home.first_frost }} · January mean low {{ region.home.jan_low_f }} °F ·
July mean high {{ region.home.jul_high_f }} °F. Frost dates are medians: about half of years
frost comes later in spring or earlier in autumn than the date printed.

## Do this now

1. **Find the current month below and do that month's items.** Do not wait for January.
2. **Put the four anchors (below) on the family calendar now.** One spring and one autumn
   weekend each for the kit check and inventory, plus a blackout weekend in each.
3. **Add the four quarterly sittings** (table below) to the same calendar: one entry each.
4. **Write your frost dates on → 25-01**; the garden half of this calendar hangs off them.
5. **Log everything you actually do** on → 24-01, with the date.

## The four anchors: these are not optional

| When | What | Page |
|---|---|---|
| **A spring weekend** (pick one: ______) | Kit check: expiry dates, batteries{{#if has.child}}, **children's sizes**{{/if}}; rotate food and water | → 22-03 |
| **An autumn weekend** (pick one: ______) | The same check, plus {{#if is.cold_winters}}the winter vehicle kits go in{{else}}vehicle kits refreshed for your hazard season{{/if}} | → 22-05 |
| **The same two weekends** | Full household inventory; work out the runways again | → 22-04, → 23-02 |
| **Spring and autumn** | **A blackout weekend**: the most useful single exercise in this binder | → 24-04 |

Everything else on this page is a seasonal chance. **These four dates carry the weight.** A
trick that works: tie them to the weekends the clocks change.

## The quarterly sittings: one calendar entry, not five

Several pages ask for something "every quarter". As separate reminders they all lapse; folded
onto the two anchor weekends plus two more evenings, they are four sittings a year. The method
for each lives on its own page; this table only schedules it.

| Every quarter | What gets done | Page |
|---|---|---|
| **Power station check**{{#if !has.power_station}} (if you get one){{/if}} | Run each station down and back up as its manual says; note the charge you found it at (a rough health check); store it at the charge level the manual gives. **Before a forecast storm or a trip away, charge to full** | → 09-03 |
| **Shielded-spares check** | Confirm spare electronics stored in shielded bags or a metal box still hold a charge; reseal | → 27-03 |
| **Children re-measured**{{#if !has.child}} (if children join the household){{/if}} | Height, weight, current sizes into the ledger; check the next sizes fit the season ahead | → 11-09 |
| **Room-by-room safety walk** | At a small child's eye level: button batteries, cords, fuel, chemicals, medicines. **Children do not have access to firearms, fuel, medications or chlorine products.** | → 20-02 |

In the two anchor months these ride the anchor weekend; in the other two quarters they get their
own evening. The yearly review (→ 25-10) checks one thing about this table: **that all four
quarters actually happened.**

## Which check matters most where you live

{{#if is.cold_winters}}**Winter is the season that kills people where you live.** The autumn check is the one that
has to be right: boots and layers that fit, vehicle kits in, wood stacked and dry, carbon
monoxide alarms tested, the heating plan rehearsed. **Do it before the first hard freeze, not
after** (NWS, Winter Weather Safety).
{{/if}}{{#if is.hot_summers}}**Summer heat is a serious hazard where you live.** The spring check is the one that has to be
right: cooling plan, shade, water stored before the heat, medicines that spoil in heat, fans
on battery (→ 11-08, → 17-04).
{{/if}}{{#if is.hurricane_region}}**Hurricane season** runs through summer and autumn on the Atlantic and Gulf coasts. Finish
the spring check and the evacuation plan before it starts (→ 17-13).
{{/if}}{{#if is.tornado_region}}**Tornado season** peaks in spring in much of the country. Run the shelter drill before it
(→ 24-02, → 17-02).
{{/if}}{{#if is.wildfire_region}}**Wildfire season** peaks in the dry months. Clear around the house and rehearse the
evacuation before them (→ 17-14).
{{/if}}{{#if is.flood_region}}**Floods** come with snowmelt, spring storms and tropical rain. Know your route to higher
ground before the wet season (→ 17-03).
{{/if}}Your top hazards from the region data: {{#each region.home.hazards as h}}{{h.name}} ({{h.rating_text}}); {{/each}}see → 17-01 and the region appendix.

## The calendar

Months are for the continental US. If your winters are mild, move the cold-weather items to
your coldest month and spend the winter months on the garden.

### Winter: December, January, February

{{#if is.cold_winters}}The hardest season, so the best training: everything you practise now is practised in real
conditions.{{else}}Your winters are mild by national standards. Use them for indoor skills and the cool-season
garden, and still practise one cold night.{{/if}}

| Month | Practise |
|---|---|
| **December** | **Cook a full meal outdoors in the cold** (→ 07-01): the most instructive session of the year. Test the one-room heating plan for a night (→ 08-01). Run the lighting plan through the longest nights (→ 10-01, → 10-06). Winter drill: the grab-and-go in coats and boots (→ 24-02) |
| **January** | {{#if is.snow_region}}**Melt snow for water** and measure how much fuel a gallon costs (→ 03-06). {{/if}}Practise layering while working outside on a cold day (→ 11-01, → 11-03). {{#if is.cold_winters}}Ice fishing, with its safety margin (→ 05-08). {{/if}}**Sharpening season**: everything gets an edge (→ 16-02). **Order seed now** (→ 05-03) |
| **February** | **Sprouts** for fresh food in the leanest month (→ 04-16). **Start slow seeds indoors**, counting back from your last frost ({{ region.home.last_frost }}) by the packet's weeks (→ 05-14, → 25-01). Sewing and repair, the indoor skills (→ 16-04, → 11-07). Re-score the checklist (→ 24-01). {{#if has.firearms}}Firearm cleaning and spare-parts count (→ 14-05, → 14-06){{/if}} |

{{#if is.cold_winters}}**Things to learn while winter is real:** how long the house holds heat with no furnace, how fast
{{#if has.child}}the children{{else}}people{{/if}} get cold, how much wood or fuel a day really costs, how batteries behave in deep
cold (→ 09-05, → 09-07), and how much harder every task is with cold hands.{{/if}}

### Spring: March, April, May

The build season: soil, seed, systems, and the year's biggest kit reset.

| Month | Practise |
|---|---|
| **March** | Start seeds; build or repair beds; turn the compost (→ 05-11). **Test the rain catchment** before the rains (→ 03-05). **Storm shelter drill** (→ 24-02, → 17-02). Service tools{{#if has.generator}} and the generator (→ 09-15){{/if}} |
| **April** | ★ **Kit check and inventory** if this is your spring anchor (→ 22-03, → 22-04). ★ **Blackout weekend** (→ 24-04). Sow cool-season crops (peas, spinach, lettuce, radish) **as soon as the soil can be worked, before the last frost**: tolerating cold is what makes them cool-season (University of Minnesota Extension, Planting the Vegetable Garden; → 05-01, → 25-01). {{#if has.pool}}Clean and test the pool system before it fills (→ 03-03, → 03-08).{{/if}} |
| **May** | Plant warm-season crops **after the last frost** ({{ region.home.last_frost }} median; wait if the year runs cold); set up season extension (→ 05-02). **Test your solar setup at good sun** and record the numbers (→ 09-09). Bicycle maintenance (→ 16-09). {{#if has.firearms}}Confirm sights at distance in decent weather (→ 14-09).{{/if}} |

### Summer: June, July, August

The production season, and the season for anything that needs sun or warm hands.

| Month | Practise |
|---|---|
| **June** | **Solar cooking** (→ 07-03). A night camped in the yard, fully off-grid{{#if has.child}}, with the children{{/if}} (→ 24-04). Run the water treatment chain on real pond or river water (→ 03-04, → 03-07). {{#if has.pool}}Mosquito control on the pool (→ 03-08).{{/if}} |
| **July** | {{#if has.pool}}**Distil pool water** properly once and taste it (→ 03-03). {{/if}}Practise heat management{{#if has.child}} for the children{{/if}}{{#if has.refrigerated_meds}} and for refrigerated medicines (→ 29-07, → 12-21){{/if}} (→ 11-08). Radio field practice and antennas (→ 15-06) |
| **August** | **Preserving season**: water-bath and pressure canning of the real harvest by tested processes (National Center for Home Food Preservation; → 04-04, → 04-05). **Low-acid foods are pressure-canned to the published time and pressure, or not canned.** Drying (→ 04-06). Fermenting (→ 04-08). **Save seed** (→ 05-03). Start the autumn wood work: **wood cut now seasons for next winter** (→ 06-03) |

### Autumn: September, October, November

The season that decides how winter goes.

| Month | Practise |
|---|---|
| **September** | Finish preserving; **soap making** (→ 13-09). Butchering and rendering if you keep animals or hunt (→ 05-09, → 05-16). Weatherproofing: plastic film, seals, door sweeps (→ 08-03). Second seed-saving pass |
| **October** | ★ **Kit check and inventory** if this is your autumn anchor (→ 22-03, → 22-04). ★ **Blackout weekend** (→ 24-04). ★ **Vehicle kits in every vehicle** (→ 22-05). ★ **Test every carbon monoxide and smoke alarm** (→ 08-02). **Stack and cover the wood** (→ 06-03). Hunting season (→ 05-07). Heat and generator drill before {{#if is.cold_winters}}the first hard freeze{{else}}you need them{{/if}} (→ 24-02, drill 8). Your median first frost: {{ region.home.first_frost }} |
| **November** | **Cold-weather fire practice**: wet, windy, cold hands (→ 06-01). Confirm the heating plan and the fuel count (→ 23-02). {{#if has.child}}**Winter clothing fitting for every child**: the item that quietly runs out (→ 11-02). {{/if}}Trapping season (→ 05-15). Full fire-and-exit drill in the dark (→ 24-02) |

## The wood calendar: the one with a one-year lag

{{figure fig-wood-year-lag}}

| When | What | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **Late winter to early spring** | Fell and cut to length | Easier hauling on frozen ground; less sap |
| **Spring** | Split | Split wood starts drying at the right time of year |
| **Summer** | Stack off the ground, covered on top, open on the sides | This is where the drying happens |
| **Autumn** | Move a winter's worth close to the house | You will not want to haul it in the coldest month |
| **Winter** | Burn **last year's** wood | **Wood cut this year is next year's fuel** (MU Extension, Wood Fuel for Heating; → 06-03, → 06-04) |

**Take the lag to heart.** It is why "we will cut wood when we need it" fails, and it is the
strongest single reason to start the wood cycle now (→ 23-04).

## The garden calendar (short version)

Full detail is on → 25-01, built from your zone ({{ region.home.zone }}) and frost dates. The
rhythm in most of the country:
- **Midwinter:** order seed; start onions and slow crops indoors.
- **Some weeks before the last frost** (the seed packet gives the number for each crop): start
  warm-season transplants indoors; sow cool crops outside as soon as the soil can be worked, **before** the last frost.
- **After the last frost** ({{ region.home.last_frost }}): warm-season transplants go out.
- **Summer:** sow in succession, water, preserve as things come in.
- **Late summer:** save seed; plant garlic and cover crops; last plantings under cover.
- **After the first frost** ({{ region.home.first_frost }}): clean up, mulch, compost, and **plan
  next year while it is fresh.**

## The year's plan on one page

```
YEAR: ______
Q1 (Jan-Mar)  skills: ______________________  drill: ____________  done: ____
Q2 (Apr-Jun)  skills: ______________________  drill: ____________  done: ____
Q3 (Jul-Sep)  skills: ______________________  drill: ____________  done: ____
Q4 (Oct-Dec)  skills: ______________________  drill: ____________  done: ____

ANCHORS:  Spring kit + inventory ____   Autumn kit + inventory ____
          Spring blackout ____          Autumn blackout ____
BIGGEST GAP FROM LAST YEAR'S REVIEW (25-10): ______________________________
```

## What you need

A **wall calendar or a set of repeating phone reminders** (the whole page fails without one), a
notebook for results, and each season's supplies bought **before** the season: seed in midwinter,
canning lids before summer, wood in spring{{#if has.child}}, children's winter gear in late
summer{{/if}}, while it is all in stock and cheap.

No money? Any calendar works. **The substitute for a calendar is a habit tied to something you
already do**: the kit check on the weekend the clocks change, seed ordering on the first snow
day.

## When it runs out

The calendar never runs out; **the season does, and it does not come back for a year.**
- **Runway:** each item here has a window of a few weeks. **Miss the preserving month and you
  have no preserved food; miss spring and the wood is not dry next winter.**
- **Ration:** if a year is too busy, keep the **four anchors** and drop the rest.
- **Resupply:** next year. That is the whole cost of a missed window: a year.
- **Substitute:** none for the seasonal items. That is why this is a calendar and not a to-do
  list: a list can slip a month; a season cannot.

## By phase

- **A, at home:** run the full calendar. Every year you do, the binder gets more accurate and
  the household gets faster.
- **B, moving:** the calendar pauses, but **the season you move in decides almost everything**
  about whether it works (→ 01-02). Moving in deep winter{{#if has.child}} with small
  children{{/if}} is a very different thing from moving in late spring.
- **C, establishing:** the calendar becomes the work of life: wood, garden, preserving, repair,
  repeat. It stops being practice and becomes the year.
